`]` `}` `}` `}` `]` `}` Erasure coding (EC) is a data storage mode used by Object Storage Service (OSS). Compared with triplicate storage, EC can provide higher data reliability at lower data redundancy levels.

**EC**

EC involves the following two concepts: Data fragments (N): Data is divided into N data fragments. Parity fragments (M): M parity fragments are computed based on the N data fragments. The N data fragments and M parity fragments that reside on different servers compose an EC group. If the number of lost data fragments is less than or equal to M, the lost segments can be restored based on the EC algorithm. We recommend that you configure the values of N and M based on the number of servers. If you have 6 to 7 servers, we recommend that you set the value of N to 2 and the value of M to 2. If you have 8 to 13 servers, we recommend that you set the value of N to 4 and the value of M to 2. If you have 14 servers or more, we recommend that you set the value of N to 8 and the value of M to 3. EC allows a server to store more than one chunk. In this case, you can store data without N + M servers. However, this reduces data security. EC allows a server to store up to M chunks. Therefore, M chunks may be lost when one server fails. EC can only ensure that data is not lost when one server fails. Apsara Stack uses a flat design in which a linear address space is divided into slices. A slice is called a chunk. Each chunk is replicated into three replicas stored on different data nodes of a storage cluster to ensure data reliability. Triplicate storage involves three key components: the master, chunk servers, and the client. Chunk servers are data nodes on which chunk replicas are stored. Each write operation is executed by the client in the following steps:
1. The client receives your write request and determines which chunk corresponds to the write operation.
2. The client queries the master to find the chunk servers on which the three replicas of the chunk are stored.
3. The client sends write requests to the chunk servers based on the result returned from the master.
4. If the write operation succeeds on all the three chunk replicas, the client returns a success message. Otherwise, the client returns a failure message.
The master ensures that the replicas of each chunk are distributed to different chunk servers across different racks. This prevents data unavailability caused by the failure of a single chunk server or rack. The distribution strategy of the master takes many factors of the storage system into account, such as chunk server disk usage, chunk server distribution across racks, power distribution conditions, and node workloads.

**Comparison between EC and triplicate storage**

Compared with triplicate storage, EC is a better solution in terms of storage usage and data reliability.

| Item | EC | Triplicate storage |
|---|---|---|
| Storage usage | The storage usage is calculated by using the following formula: N/(N + M) . For example, the storage usage in EC storage mode of the 8+3 configuration is 8/(8 + 3) = 72.7%. | 1/3=33.3% |

| Reliability | Allows up to M fragments to be lost. Failures on up to M servers are allowed in the worst case. For example, failures on up to 3 servers are allowed in EC storage mode of the 8+3 configuration. | Allows up to two replicas to be lost. Failures on up to two servers are allowed in the worst case. |
|---|---|---|

OSS supports the Write Once Read Many (WORM) feature that prevents an object from being deleted or overwritten for a specified period of time. The WORM feature is not available in the OSS console.

**Prerequisites**

Versioning is not enabled for the bucket for which you want to configure a retention policy.

**Scenarios**

OSS provides strong compliance policies. You can configure time-based retention policies for buckets. After you configure and lock a retention policy for a bucket, objects that are uploaded to the bucket and the retention policy cannot be deleted within the retention period. You can delete the objects only after the retention period ends. The WORM feature is widely used in sectors such as finance, insurance, health care, and securities, and in scenarios such as Multi-Layer Protection Scheme (MLPS) audit of log data. The WORM feature helps you meet your bucket compliance requirements. You can configure retention policies only for buckets in OSS. During the retention period, you can configure lifecycle rules to convert the storage classes of the objects in the bucket. This way, you can reduce storage costs and ensure compliance.

**Rule description**

You can configure only a single time-based retention policy for each bucket. The policy specifies a retention period that ranges from 1 day to 70 years. For example, assume that you created a bucket named examplebucket on June 1, 2013, and uploaded the file1.txt, file2.txt, and file3.txt objects to the bucket at different points in time. On July 1, 2014, you created a retention policy for the bucket and specified a five-year retention period. The following table describes the upload and expiration dates of the objects.

| Object name | Upload date | Expiration date |
|---|---|---|
| file1.txt | June 1, 2013 | May 31, 2018 |
| file2.txt | July 1, 2014 | June 30, 2019 |
| file3.txt | September 30, 2018 | September 29, 2023 |

Policy effects After a time-based retention policy is created, the policy remains in the InProgress state for 24 hours. The retention policy protects the specified resources in the bucket within 24 hours after the policy is created. Within 24 hours after the retention policy is created: If the retention policy is not locked, the bucket owner and authorized users can delete the policy. If the retention policy is locked, the retention period of the policy cannot be shortened and the policy cannot be deleted. The retention period can only be extended. 24 hours after the retention policy is created: If the retention policy is not locked, the policy becomes invalid. If you attempt to delete or modify data in the protected bucket, a `409 FileImmutable` error is returned. Deletion A time-based retention policy is a metadata attribute of a bucket. If a bucket is deleted, the retention policy and the access control list (ACL) of the bucket are also deleted. If a bucket is empty, the bucket owner can delete the bucket. The retention policy of the bucket is also deleted. If the retention policy is not locked within 24 hours after the policy is created, the bucket owner and authorized users can delete the policy. If a bucket contains objects that are protected within the retention period, you cannot delete the bucket or the retention policy. Object Storage Service (OSS) slices user data and discretely stores the sliced data in a distributed file system based on specific rules. The user data and its indexes are stored separately. OSS uses symmetric AccessKey pairs to authenticate users and verifies the signature in each HTTP request sent by users. If verification is successful, OSS reassembles the distributed data. This way, OSS implements data storage isolation between different tenants. Object Storage Service (OSS) provides multiple disaster recovery capabilities to ensure data security and improve availability. To ensure data availability, OSS provides the following disaster recovery capabilities.

| Capability | Description |
|---|---|

| Zone-disaster recovery | Zone-disaster recovery allows you to store multiple replicas of your data in multiple zones within the same region. This feature prevents data loss and helps you recover your business if a single zone fails. OSS provides two zone-disaster recovery solutions: Two-zone disaster recovery: After zone-disaster recovery is enabled for buckets, data is replicated from the bucket in the primary data center to the secondary bucket in the OSS cluster in the secondary data center. In this case, objects in the bucket remain accessible even if the primary data center fails due to reasons such as power outages and fire. To address the growing demands for high traffic and concurrency while ensuring high availability and disaster recovery capabilities, OSS allows you to deploy multiple independent two-zone disaster recovery clusters within the same region. These clusters work together to handle business traffic, enabling elastic resource scaling and risk isolation. Three-zone disaster recovery: After you create a bucket and configure zone-redundant storage for the bucket,y our data is stored across three zones in the same region. If one of the three zones fails due toa network disconnection, power outage, or disaster event, the other two zones remain available to ensure business continuity and data security. If a single zone fails, OSS can still provide strong-consistency services. This way, the failover process is imperceptible, and your data is not lost during failovers. This also helps meet the strict requirements of key business systems for which the recovery time objective (RTO) and the recovery point objective (RPO) must be zero. |
|---|---|
| Cross-region replication (CRR) | CRR allows you to automatically and asynchronously (in near real-time) replicate objects in a bucket from one region to a bucket in a different region within the same account or a different account. CRR replicates operations, such as the creation, overwriting, and deletion of objects, from a source bucket to a destination bucket. |
| Cross-cloud replication | The cross-cloud replication feature allows you to replicate data from one cloud to another cloud. This way, you can back up data across clouds. If a cloud fails, you can switch over your business to another cloud to ensure business continuity. |
| Three data centers across two regions | If your business has high requirements on data backup, you can use the zone-disaster recovery and CRR features to build a disaster recovery solution based on three data centers across two regions. |

By default, the access control list (ACL) of Object Storage Service (OSS) resources, including buckets and objects, is set to private to ensure data security. Only the bucket owner and authorized users can access these resources. OSS allows you to configure a variety of policies to grant third-party users specific permissions to access or use your OSS resources. OSS provides the following access permission policies.

| Policy | Description |
|---|---|
| RAM Policy | Resource Access Management (RAM) is a service provided by Alibaba Cloud to manage access permissions on resources. RAM policies are configured based on users. You can manage users by configuring RAM policies. For users such as employees, systems, or applications, you can control which resources are accessible. For example, you can create a RAM policy to grant users only read permissions on a bucket. |
| Bucket Policy | A bucket policy is a resource-based authorization policy. Compared with RAM policies, bucket policies can be easily configured by using GUI in the console. In addition, the owner of a bucket can configure bucket policies for the bucket without RAM permissions. You can configure bucket policies to grant permissions to the RAM users of other Apsara Stack accounts or anonymous users who access OSS by using the specified IP addresses. |
| Bucket ACL | You can configure the ACL of a bucket when you create the bucket or modify the ACL of a created bucket. Only the owner of a bucket can configure or modify the ACL of the bucket. You can set the ACL of a bucket to one of the following values: Public Read/Write, Public-Read, and Private. |
| Object ACL | You can also configure the ACL of each object stored in OSS. You can configure the ACL of an object when you upload the object or modify the ACL of an uploaded object based on your requirements. You can set the ACL of an object to one of the following values: Inherited from bucket, Public Read/Write, Public-Read, and Private. |
| Hotlink protection | You can configure a Referer whitelist for a bucket to prevent your resources in the bucket from unauthorized access. |
| CORS | Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) is a standard cross-origin solution provided by HTML5 to allow web application servers to control cross-origin access, which ensures the security of data transmission across origins. |

Object Storage Service (OSS) supports server-side encryption. When you upload an object to a bucket for which server-side encryption is enabled, OSS encrypts the object and stores the encrypted object. When you download the encrypted object from OSS, OSS automatically decrypts the object and returns the decrypted object to you. In addition, a header is added in the response to indicate that the object is encrypted on the OSS server.

**Encryption methods**

OSS protects static data by using server-side encryption. You can use this method in scenarios in which additional security or compliance is required, such as the storage of deep learning samples and online collaborative documents. You can use SSE-OSS to encrypt all your objects. To improve security, OSS uses master keys that are rotated on a regular basis to encrypt data keys. You can use this method to encrypt and decrypt multiple objects at a time.

**Server-side encryption by using OSS-managed keys**

OSS generates and manages data keys used to encrypt data, and provides strong and multi-factor security measures to protect data. OSS server-side encryption uses AES-256, which is one of the advanced encryption standard algorithms, and SM4, which is one of the Chinese cryptographic algorithms. Use the following configuration methods: Configure the default server-side encryption method for a bucket Set the default encryption method to SSE-OSS and specify the encryption algorithm as AES-256 . This way, all objects uploaded to this bucket are encrypted. Configure an encryption method for a specific object When you upload an object or modify the metadata of an object, include the `x-oss-server-side-encryption` parameter in the request and set the parameter value to `AES-265` or `SM4` . This way, the object is encrypted by using SSE-OSS. Client-side encryption encrypts objects locally before uploading them to Object Storage Service (OSS).

**Disclaimers**

When using client-side encryption, you are responsible for the integrity and correctness of your master key. Incorrect use or loss of the master key due to improper maintenance will result in data loss and other consequences if encrypted data cannot be decrypted. You bear all such losses and consequences. When copying or migrating encrypted data, you are responsible for the integrity and correctness of the encryption metadata. Errors or loss of encryption metadata due to improper maintenance will result in data loss and other consequences if encrypted data cannot be decrypted. You bear all such losses and consequences.

**How it works**

When using client-side encryption, a random data key (DK) is generated for each object. The plaintext data key symmetrically encrypts the object’s data. The master key is used to generate this random data key. The encrypted data key is stored as object metadata on the server. To decrypt the object, the master key first decrypts the encrypted data key. The resulting plaintext data key then decrypts the object’s data. The master key participates only in local client-side computations and is neither transmitted over the network nor stored on the server, ensuring its security. Two methods are supported for master key usage: KMS-managed customer master keys and customer-managed CMKs.

**Using KMS-Managed Customer Master Keys**

When using KMS-managed customer master keys for client-side data encryption, do not provide any encryption keys to the OSS encryption client. Instead, specify the KMS customer master key (CMK) ID when uploading objects. The following diagram illustrates how it works. Encrypt and upload objects i. Obtain encryption keys. Using the CMK ID, the client sends a request to KMS to obtain a data key (DK) for object encryption. In response, KMS returns a randomly generated plaintext data key (DK) and an encrypted data key. ii. Encrypt data and upload to OSS. After receiving the plaintext and encrypted data keys from KMS, the local client uses the plaintext data key to perform local encryption. It then uploads the encrypted object and the encrypted data key to OSS. Download and decrypt objects i. Download the object. The client downloads the encrypted object and the encrypted data key—stored as object metadata—from the OSS server. ii. Decrypt objects. The client sends the encrypted data key and CMK ID to the KMS server. In response, KMS decrypts the data key using the specified CMK and returns the plaintext data key to the local encryption client. The local encryption client obtains a unique data key for each uploaded object. To ensure data security, rotate or update the CMK regularly. Maintain the mapping between the CMK ID and the object.

**Using Customer-Managed CMKs**

When using customer-managed CMKs, you must generate and securely store the encryption keys yourself. When the local client encrypts an object, you provide the encryption key—either a symmetric key or an asymmetric key—to the local encryption client. The following diagram illustrates the encryption process. Encrypt and upload objects i. Provide the local encryption client with a customer master key (either a symmetric key or an asymmetric key). ii. The local encryption client generates a one-time symmetric data key (DK) locally. This key encrypts a single object, and a new data key is randomly generated for each object. iii. The client uses the data key to encrypt the object and the provided master key to encrypt the data key. iv. The client uploads the encrypted data key as part of the object metadata to OSS. Download and decrypt objects i. The client downloads the encrypted object and its metadata from OSS. ii. Using the information in the metadata, the client authorizes the use of the corresponding master key to decrypt the data key, then uses the decrypted data key to decrypt the object.

**Important**

The OSS local encryption client does not send the customer master key or unencrypted data to OSS. Therefore, store encryption keys securely. If a key is lost, you cannot decrypt the data. The local encryption client randomly generates data keys. Client-side encryption supports multipart upload for objects larger than 5 GiB. When using multipart upload, specify the total object size and shard size. All shards, except the last one, must be the same size, and the shard size must be a multiple of 16. After uploading an object using client-side encryption, the encryption metadata is protected. You cannot modify object metadata using CopyObject. Communication between client applications and Object Storage Service (OSS) is encrypted by using the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. TLS is a standard cryptographic protocol that ensures privacy and data integrity between clients and servers that communicate over the Internet. After you configure the TLS version and the cipher suite on an OSS client, the client can use only the configured TLS version to send requests to and receive requests from OSS to ensure communication security.

**TLS versions**

The TLS protocol supports the following versions: TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, TLS 1.2, and TLS 1.3. OSS supports only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The following table describes the applicable scenarios of each version and the mainstream browsers that support each version.

| Protocol version | Description | Applicable scenario | Supported browser |
|---|---|---|---|
| TLS 1.2 | TLS 1.2 further enhances security for network connections, and launches new features, such as Server Name Indication (SNI) and handshake protocols. TLS 1.2 supports more encryption algorithms, including AES-GCM, AES-CBC, and ECDHE. | TLS 1.2 is suitable for most common secure communication scenarios, including web applications, e-commerce websites, emails, and virtual private networks (VPNs). | IE11+ Chrome 30+ Firefox 27+ Safri 7+ |

| TLS 1.3 | TLS 1.3 significantly improves security, performance, and privacy. TLS 1.3 no longer supports some insecure encryption algorithms. It supports more powerful key exchange algorithms and encryption algorithms that reduce the delay of the handshake process, and also provides better forward secrecy and authentication mechanisms. | TLS 1.3 is suitable for scenarios in which high security, better performance, and privacy protection are required, such as in financial institutions, large Internet companies, and government agencies. | Chrome 70+ Firefox 63+ |
|---|---|---|---|

If you disable TLS version management, TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are supported by default. If you enable TLS version management, you can select TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. Downgrading the TLS version, such as changing the TLS version from TLS 1.3 to TLS 1.2, or disabling TLS version management may cause security and compliance issues. Proceed with caution when you perform the operation. Before you disable a TLS version, make sure that it is not the only version used by clients. You can set the TLS version by using OSS SDK for Java.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **TLS Version Management** section, click **Settings**.
4. Turn on **TLS Version Management**, and select an allowed TLS version.
5. Click **Save**.
After you specify a TLS version, the clients can use only the TLS version to send requests to and receive requests from OSS. This improves communication security. OSS allows you to configure versioning for a bucket to protect objects that are stored in the bucket. After you enable versioning for a bucket, data that is overwritten or deleted in the bucket is saved as a previous version. After you configure versioning for a bucket, you can recover objects in the bucket to any previous version to protect your data from being accidentally overwritten or deleted.

**Versioning states**

A bucket can be in one of the following versioning states: disabled, enabled, and suspended. By default, versioning is disabled for a bucket. After versioning is enabled for a bucket, the versioning state of the bucket cannot be set back to disabled. However, you can suspend versioning for a bucket that has versioning enabled. When an object is uploaded to a bucket for which versioning is enabled, OSS generates a random string as the globally unique version ID of the object. When an object is uploaded to a bucket for which versioning is suspended, OSS generates the "null" string as the version ID of the object.

**Scenarios**

To ensure data security, we recommend that you use versioning in the following scenarios: Recover deleted data You can configure versioning to recover deleted data. Recover overwritten data Numerous temporary versions are created in scenarios where modifications are frequently made, such as online collaborative documents and documents stored in online storage. You can use the versioning feature to retrieve a specified version of an object stored in the bucket.

**Data protection**

The following table describes how OSS processes deleted and overwritten data in buckets in different versioning states to help you understand the data protection mechanism of versioning.

| Versioning state | Object overwriting | Object deletion |
|---|---|---|
| Disabled | The existing object is overwritten and cannot be recovered. Only the current object version is retained in the bucket. | The object is deleted and cannot be accessed. |
| Enabled | A new version with a unique ID is generated for the object. The existing object is stored as a previous version. | A delete marker with a globally unique version ID is added to the object as the current version. The existing object is stored as a previous version. |
| Suspended | A new version whose version ID is null is generated for the object. If the object already has a previous version or delete marker whose version ID is null, the previous version or delete marker is overwritten by the new null version. Other previous versions or delete markers whose version IDs are not null are not affected. | A delete marker whose version ID is null is added to the object. If the object already has a previous version or delete marker whose version ID is null, the previous version or delete marker is overwritten by the new delete marker. Other previous versions or delete markers whose version IDs are not null are not affected. |

The following examples provide figures to show how OSS processes data when an object with the same name as an existing object is uploaded to or an object is deleted from a bucket for which versioning is enabled or suspended. All version IDs in the figures are in the simple format for readability. Overwrite an object in a versioning-enabled bucket When you upload an object repeatedly to a versioning-enabled bucket, the object is overwritten in each upload. A version with a unique version ID is generated for the object each time when the object is overwritten. Delete an object from a versioning-enabled bucket When you delete an object from a versioning-enabled bucket, OSS adds a delete marker to the object as the current version of the object instead of permanently deleting this object. The previous versions of the object are not deleted. If you upload an object with the same name after the delete marker is added, a new version with a unique version ID is added as the current version. Overwrite an object in a versioning-suspended bucket When you upload an object with the same name as an existing object in a bucket for which versioning is suspended, a new version whose version ID is null is added and the previous versions of the object are retained. If you upload another object with the same name to the bucket again, a new version whose version ID is null overwrites the current version whose version ID is null. Delete an object from a versioning-suspended bucket When you delete an object from a bucket for which versioning is suspended, OSS adds a delete marker to the object as the current version of the object instead of permanently deleting this object. The previous versions of the object are not deleted. In a versioning-enabled bucket, deleted and overwritten data is stored as previous versions. After you enable versioning for a bucket, you can recover objects in the bucket to a previous version to protect your data from being accidentally overwritten or deleted. You can add Image Processing (IMG) parameters to GetObject requests to process image objects stored in Object Storage Service (OSS). For example, you can add image watermarks to images or convert image formats. OSS allows you to use one or more parameters to process images, or encapsulate multiple IMG parameters in a style to process images. When multiple IMG parameters are included in a request, OSS processes the image in the order of the parameters. You can use object URLs, API operations, and OSS SDKs to process images. The following table describes the IMG operations supported by OSS.

| IMG operation | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Resize images | resize | Resizes images to a specified size. |
| Incircle | circle | Crops images based on the center point of images to rounds of a specified size. |
| Custom crop | crop | Crops images to rectangles of a specified size. |
| Indexed cut | indexcrop | Cuts images along a specified horizontal or vertical axis and selects one of the cut images. |
| Rounded rectangle | rounded-corners | Crops images to rounded rectangles based on the specified rounded corner size. |
| Automatic rotation | auto-orient | Auto-rotates images for which the auto-orient parameter is configured. |
| Rotate | rotate | Rotates images clockwise at a specified angle. |
| Blur | blur | Blurs images. |
| Adjust brightness | bright | Adjusts the brightness of images. |
| Sharpen | sharpen | Sharpens images. |
| Adjust contrast | contrast | Adjusts the contrast of images. |
| Gradual display | interlace | Configures gradual display for the JPG images. |
| Adjust image quality | quality | Adjusts the quality of JPG and WebP images. |
| Convert format | format | Converts image formats. |
| Add watermarks | watermark | Adds image or text watermarks to images. |
| Query average tone | average-hue | Queries the average tone of images. |
| Query image information | info | Queries image information, including basic information and Exchangeable Image File Format (EXIF) information. |

This topic describes the parameters that you can configure to capture video snapshots and provides examples. When you capture video snapshots, you are charged based on the number of captured images. Object Storage Service (OSS) can capture images from video objects only in the H.264 and H.265 formats. By default, OSS does not automatically store captured images. You must manually download the captured images to your local storage devices.

**Parameters**

Operation type: `video` Operation name: **snapshot**

| Paramete r | Description | Valid value |
|---|---|---|
| t | Specifies the time when the image is to be captured. | [0, video duration] Unit: ms |
| w | Specifies the width based on which to capture the image. If this parameter is set to 0, the width of the image to capture is automatically calculated. | [0, video width] Unit: px |
| h | Specifies the height based on which to capture the image. If this parameter is set to 0, the height of the image to capture is automatically calculated. If both w and h are set to 0, the width and height of the source image are used as those of image to capture. | [0, video height] Unit: px |
| m | Specifies the mode used to capture the image. If this parameter is not specified, the image is captured in the default mode. In other words, the image at the specified point of time in the video is captured. If this parameter is set to fast, the most recent key frame before the specified time is captured. | fast |
| f | Specifies the format of the captured image. | jpg and png |
| ar | Specifies whether to automatically rotate the image based on the video information. If this parameter is set to auto, the system automatically rotates the image based on the video information. | auto |

**Examples**

Use the fast mode to capture the image at the seventh second of the video. Export the captured image as a JPG image with the width of 800 px and height of 600 px. The URL of the processed image is in the following format: <Source video URL>?x-oss-process=video/snapshot,t_7000,f_jpg,w_800,h_600,m_fast Use the default mode to capture the image at the fiftieth second of the video accurately. Export it as a JPG image with the width of 800 px and height of 600 px. The URL of the processed image is in the following format: <Source video URL>?x-oss-process=video/snapshot,t_50000,f_jpg,w_800,h_600

### 2.2 Notes

This topic describes key considerations before you use Object Storage Service (OSS).

**Important**

Do not directly access OSS using the virtual IP address (VIP) of the OSS cluster because the VIP is dynamic and poses security risks. If other users need to use some or all OSS features, you can create a Resource Access Management (RAM) user and grant the user the required RAM permissions. This ensures that the user has operation permissions consistent with their RAM policy to access or manage OSS. Before using OSS, also note the following limitations:

| Limitation | Description |
|---|---|
| Buckets | A user can create a maximum of 100 buckets. After you create a bucket, you cannot change its name or region. |
| Upload objects | Objects uploaded through the console, simple upload, form upload, or append upload cannot exceed 5 GiB. To upload objects larger than 5 GiB, use multipart upload. Objects uploaded using multipart upload cannot exceed 48.8 TiB. OSS supports uploading objects with the same name, but this overwrites existing objects. |
| Delete objects | You cannot recover objects after deletion. The console limits batch deletion to 100 objects. For larger batch deletions, use an API or software development kit (SDK). |
| Lifecycle | Each bucket's lifecycle configuration can contain a maximum of 1,000 rules. |

Click the Single Tunnels block to go to the SingleTunnel List page to view existing single tunnels. |
| Total Bucket capacity | In the Total Bucket capacity section, view the percentages of allocated bucket capacity and used bucket capacity. |
| Top 10 organizations | In the Top 10 organizations section, view the top 10 organizations with the highest capacity usage or capacity allocation rate. |

Specify a metric, sort order, metric value, and number of top buckets to display and clickS earch to view resources sorted based on the specified metric and order. Click the name of a bucket to view the bucket details. |
| Alarm Statistics | In the Alarm Statistics section, view the total number of alerts, number of alerts of each severity level, and list of alerts. On the right-side tabs of different severity levels, view the following information: Instance ID/Name, Organization/Resource Set, Alarm Rule ID, Alarm Content, and Time. |

This topic describes how to log on to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.

**Prerequisites**

The URL of the console that is obtained from the deployment personnel. A supported browser is used. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.
1. Enter the URL of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console in the address bar and press the Enter key.
2. On the login page, enter your username and password.
You can obtain the username and password that are used to log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console from the operations administrator.

**First login**

The first time that you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you need to change the password of your account. The password must be 10 to 32 characters in length. It must contain all of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Supported special characters include: ! @ # $ %

**Forgotten password**

If you have forgotten your password, click Forgot Password. On the page that appears, enter the username of your account, the email address that was used to create the account, and the CAPTCHA code. Then, the system sends a link for resetting the password to the specified email address.
3. Click **Log On**.
4. If multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for your account, perform operations based on your logon scenarios:
Scenario 1: This is your first time logging on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console after MFA is enabled by the administrator. a. On the Bind Virtual MFA Device page, bind an MFA device as prompted. b. Enter the username and password again as in Step 2 and click **Log On**. c. Enter the six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**. Scenario 2: You log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console after MFA is enabled and an MFA device is bound. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**. For more information, see the **Bind a virtual MFA device to enable MFA** topic in **Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User**
**Guide**.
5. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Storage** > **Object Storage Service**.
Objects uploaded to Object Storage Service (OSS) are stored in buckets. To upload data to OSS, you must first create an OSS bucket. This topic describes how to create an OSS bucket.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click **Create Bucket**.
3. On the **Create OSS Bucket** page, configure parameters.
OSS does not limit the number of objects in a bucket. A test has shown that a trillion objects in a bucket do not affect the read and write performance. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Organization Name | Select an organization from the drop-down list for the bucket. |
| Resource Set | Select a resource set from the drop-down list for the bucket. |

| Region | Select a region from the drop-down list for the bucket. Note The region of a bucket cannot be changed after the bucket is created. If you want to access OSS from your Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance over the internal network, select the region where your ECS instance is deployed. |
|---|---|
| Domain Name | Select the endpoint of the bucket. |
| Cluster | Select a cluster for the bucket. You can deploy multiple OSS clusters on Apsara Stack. |
| Bucket Name | Enter a name for the bucket. Note The bucket name must comply with the naming conventions. The bucket name must be globally unique among all existing buckets in OSS. The bucket name cannot be changed after the bucket is created. |
| Storage Class | Select a storage class for the bucket. Use the Standard storage class. Apsara Stack OSS supports only the Standard storage class. The Standard storage class supports zone-redundant storage (ZRS) and locally redundant storage (LRS). |
| Redundancy Type | Select the redundancy type of the bucket. LRS LRS stores multiple copies of your data on multiple devices of different facilities in the same zone. LRS provides data durability and availability even if hardware failures occur. ZRS Important This parameter is available only when three-zone disaster recovery is used. ZRS stores multiple copies of your data across multiple zones in the same region. Your data is still accessible even if a zone becomes unavailable. For more information, see Zone-redundant storage. |
| Capacity Configuration | Set Capacity Configuration and Capacity Unit, and then specify the capacity of the bucket. Capacity Configuration: Only Specified Capacity is supported. Capacity units: GiB and TiB Valid values: 1 to 2000000 TiB and 1 to 2048000000 GiB. |
| Capacity Unit |   |
| Specified Capacity |   |
| Versioning | Specify whether to enable versioning. Valid values: Enable: If you enable versioning for a bucket, objects that are overwritten or deleted in the bucket are stored as previous versions. Versioning allows you to restore objects in a bucket to a previous version and protects your data from being accidentally overwritten or deleted. Disable: If you disable versioning for a bucket, objects that are overwritten in or deleted from the bucket cannot be restored. |
| ACL | Select an access control list (ACL) for the bucket. Valid values: Important The public-read or public-read-write ACL allows users to read or write the data in your OSS buckets without authentication, which poses a high security risk. To ensure data security, we recommend that you set the ACL of all your buckets to private. Valid values: Private: Only the owner of the bucket and authorized users have read and write access to objects in the bucket. Other users, including anonymous users, do not have access to objects in the bucket. Public Read: Only the owner of the bucket has read and write access to objects in the bucket. All users, including anonymous users, have only read access to objects in the bucket. Public Read/Write: All users, including anonymous users, have read and write access to objects in the bucket. Charges generated by such operations are paid by the owner of the bucket. Exercise caution when you set the ACL to Public Read/Write. Note You can change the ACL of a bucket after the bucket is created. For more information, seeM odify bucket ACLs. |

| Server-Side Encryption | Configure server-side encryption for the bucket. Valid values: None: Server-side encryption is not performed. OSS-Managed: Keys managed by OSS are used to encrypt objects in the bucket. KMS: Customer master keys (CMKs) managed by Key Management Service (KMS) are used to encrypt objects in the bucket. |
|---|---|
| Encryption Algorithm | Select an encryption algorithm. This parameter is available only when you set the Server-Side Encryption parameter to OSS Fully Managed or KMS. Valid values: AES256: AES256 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The customer master keys (CMKs) used to encrypt the data keys are rotated regularly. SM4: SM4 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The CMKs used to encrypt the data keys are rotated regularly. |
| AccessKey Pair ID | This parameter is available only when you select KMS for Server-Side Encryption. OSS uses the specified CMK to encrypt objects in the bucket. Note If no CMK is available, you must create one in the KMS console. |
| Disable Zone-disaster Recovery | Select whether to enable zone-disaster recovery for the bucket. You can configure this parameter only when you set the Redundancy Type parameter to LRS. Important This parameter is available only after disaster recovery clusters are deployed in two-zone disaster recovery scenarios. If Disable Zone-disaster Recovery is set to No, zone-disaster recovery is enabled. If zone-disaster recovery is enabled for buckets, bucket data is replicated from the primary data center to the secondary bucket in the OSS cluster in the secondary data center. In this case, objects in the bucket remain accessible even if the primary data center fails due to reasons such as power outages and fire. If Disable Zone-disaster Recovery is set to Yes, zone-disaster recovery is disabled. Objects in the bucket are stored in LRS mode. In LRS mode, the copies of each object are stored across different devices within the same zone. This way, OSS ensures data reliability and availability even if two storage devices fail at the same time. |
| KMS-based Encryption | By default, objects that are encrypted by using KMS-managed CMKs in the source bucket cannot be synchronized to the destination bucket, even if zone-disaster recovery is enabled. To synchronize objects that are encrypted by using KMS-managed CMKs to the destination bucket, you must enable KMS-based encryption, add a KMS-managed CMK for encryption and decryption, and attach a Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has permissions on object-related operations and KMS-based encryption and decryption. This parameter is available only when Disable Zone-disaster recovery is set to No. To configure KMS-based encryption, perform the following steps: i. Turn on KMS-Encrypted Object. ii. Specify CMK ID and RAM Role Name. |
| CMK ID | Select a KMS-managed CMK for object encryption and decryption. This parameter is available only whenK MS-based Encryption is turned on. Make sure that you have created a KMS CMK in the KMS console. |
| RAM Role Name | Attach a role to the OSS service. The role must have permissions to perform operations on encrypted objects and encrypt and decrypt objects by using KMS-managed CMKs. This parameter is available only when KMS-based Encryption is turned on. To attach a role that has the required permissions, you can use the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole or create a custom role. For more information about how to grant permissions to a role, see Grant permissions to a role. Use the predefined RAM role OSS provides the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole. You can click Bind Now to use this predefined role when you configure a RAM role during bucket creation. Create a custom role You can click Create Role to create a custom role. |

4. Click **Submit**.
After the bucket is created, you can view the bucket information and perform operations on the bucket as needed. To view and manage a bucket, click the name of the bucket. On the bucket details page, you can view the overview, manage objects, configure basic settings, and query logs. For example, you can go to the **Overview** tab of the bucket details page to view information about the bucket, such as the **organization and resource set**, **endpoints**, and **basic settings**. To enable versioning for a bucket, click **Enable** in the **Version control** column. For more information, see Configure versioning.

**Important**

After you enable versioning for a bucket, objects that are overwritten or deleted in the bucket are stored as previous versions. We recommend that you configure valid lifecycle rules based on your business requirements to manage objects in buckets. This prevents large volumes of data from being stored in a bucket when versioning is enabled. After you create a bucket, you can upload objects to the bucket.

**Background information**

You can upload an object of any format to a bucket. You can use the Object Storage Service (OSS) console to upload an object up to 5 GiB in size. To upload an object larger than 5 GiB, use OSS SDKs or call an API operation.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, click **Upload files**.
4. In the **Upload files** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Upload | Select the directory to which you want to upload objects. Valid values: Current Directory: The objects are uploaded to the current directory. Specify Directory: The object is uploaded to a specific directory. You must enter the name of the directory. If you specify a directory that does not exist in the bucket, OSS automatically creates the directory and uploads the object to the directory. The directory must comply with the following naming conventions: The name must contain UTF-8 characters and cannot contain emoticons. You can use forward slashes ( / ) to separate multiple paths and quickly create subdirectories. The subdirectory cannot start with a forward slash ( / ) or a backslash ( \ ), and cannot contain consecutive forward slashes ( / ). You cannot specify two consecutive periods ( .. ) as a subdirectory. The directory must be 1 to 254 characters in length. |
| File ACL | Select an ACL for the object to upload. Default value:I nherited Bucket. Inherited Bucket: The ACL of uploaded objects is the same as that of the bucket. Private: Only the owner and authorized users can read and write objects in the bucket. Other users, including anonymous users, cannot access the objects in the bucket without authorization. Public Reading: Only the bucket owner and authorized users have read and write access to objects in the bucket. Other users, including anonymous users, have only read access to objects in the bucket. Public Read/Write: All users have read and write access to objects in the bucket. |
| Upload files | Drag one or more objects to upload to this section, or click theU pload icon to select one or more objects to upload. Important If the object that you want to upload has the same name as an existing object in the bucket, the existing object is overwritten. If you upload a folder, only the files in the folder are uploaded. The files are stored in the same directory in the bucket. You cannot use the OSS console to upload an object that is greater than 5 GiB in size. If you want to upload an object that is greater than 5 GiB in size, use the OSS SDK or OSS API to perform multipart upload. The name of the object to upload must comply with the following conventions: The object name must be encoded in UTF-8. The object name is case-sensitive. The object name must be 1 to 1,023 bytes in length. The object name cannot start with a forward slash (/) or a backslash (\). |

5. In the **Upload files** panel, wait until the upload task is completed.
In the **Upload files** panel, perform operations as needed.

**Cancel upload tasks**

During the upload process, click **Cancel all** to cancel all upload tasks. Click **Cancel** in the **Operation** column to cancel the upload of a single file.

**Remove completed tasks**

After an object is uploaded, click **Remove completed** to remove all completed upload tasks. Click **Remove** in the **Operation** column to remove a single upload task.

**Important**

Do not refresh or close the **Upload Task** panel when objects are being uploaded. Otherwise, the upload tasks are interrupted. You can obtain the URL of an uploaded object and share the URL with other users to preview or download the object.

**Prerequisites**

An object is uploaded to the bucket. For more information, see Upload an object.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, obtain object URLs.
Obtain the URL of a single object Click the name of the object whose URL you want to obtain. In the **Details** panel, click **Copy file URL** below the **URL** parameter. Export multiple object URLs at the same time Select the objects that you want to export and click **Export URL list**.

### 2.5 Buckets

You can view the detailed information of buckets in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.

**Prerequisites**

An OSS bucket is created. For more information, see Create buckets.
1. Log in to the OSS console. For more information, see Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **Overview** tab, you can view the information about the bucket, including the **Organization and resource set**,**Access domain name**, and
**Basic settings**.
You can use domain names to manage a bucket over HTTP or HTTPS. You can view the storage quota of a bucket in the **Basic settings** section. For more information, see Configure the storage quota. This topic describes how to delete buckets in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.

**Prerequisites**

All objects and parts in the bucket are deleted. For more information, see Delete objects and Manage parts.

**Warning**

Deleted objects, parts, and buckets cannot be recovered. Proceed with caution.
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. Click **Delete a Bucket** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
Object Storage Service (OSS) provides the access control list (ACL) feature to control access to buckets. By default, the ACL of a bucket is private. You can modify the ACL of the bucket after it is created.

**Background information**

You can set the ACL of a bucket to one of the following values: Private: Only the bucket owner or authorized users can read and write objects in the bucket. Other users, including anonymous users, cannot access the objects in the bucket without authorization. Public-read: Only the bucket owner or authorized users can write objects in the bucket. Other users, including anonymous users, can only read objects in the bucket. Public-read-write: All users, including anonymous users, can read and write the objects in the bucket.

**Warning**

If you set the ACL of a bucket to public-read or public-read-write, other users can read the data in the bucket without authentication, which may result in security risks. To ensure data security, we recommend that you set the ACL of your bucket to private.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Read and write permissions** section, click **Settings**.
4. Select an ACL for the bucket.
5. Click **Submit**.
You can enable versioning for a bucket to protect objects stored in the bucket. When you overwrite or delete objects that are stored in a versioningenabled bucket, Object Storage Service (OSS) saves the objects as previous versions in the bucket. After you enable versioning for a bucket, you can restore objects in the bucket to a previous version to protect your data from being accidentally overwritten or deleted.

**Background information**

After versioning is enabled, OSS specifies a unique ID for each version of all objects in a bucket. You can also download a previous version of an object or restore a previous version at any time based on the version ID.

**Enable versioning**

1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to enable versioning.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Version control** section, click **Settings**.
4. Click **Activate**, and then click **Submit**.
If you no longer need more object versions in a versioning-enabled bucket, you can click **Pause**. In this case, OSS specifies that the ID of a new version is null and no more previous versions are generated. However, the existing versions are retained.

**Restore a previous version**

You can restore a specified previous version of an object as the current version.
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to enable versioning.
3. On the page that appears, click the **File management** tab. In the upper-right corner, set **Version history** to **Display**.
4. Select a previous version and click **Recovery** below the file list.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**. Then, OSS copies the specified version of the object to the current directory. The existing current version is
overwritten, and the specified previous version becomes the current version.

**Download previous versions**

You can download a specified previous version of an object.
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **File management** tab. In the upper-right corner, set **Version history** to **Display**.
4. Click the object version that you want to download. In the **Details** panel that appears, click **Download** on the right side of **File URL**.
You can also click **Details** in the **Operation** column to open this panel.
5. Select the location where you want to store the downloaded version and then click **Save**.

**Delete previous versions**

We recommend that you delete idle previous versions in a timely manner to minimize storage costs.

**Important**

Deleted previous versions cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when you perform this operation. If you delete the current version of an object, the latest previous version becomes the current version. You can also configure lifecycle rules to automatically delete previous versions on a regular basis.
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **File management** tab. In the upper-right corner, set **Version history** to **Display**.
4. Delete a one or more previous versions.
Delete a single previous version Find the version that you no longer use and click **Delete** in the **Operation** column. Delete multiple previous versions at the same time Select the previous versions that you want to delete and click **Delete completely** below the file list.
5. Click **OK**.
Object Storage Service (OSS) supports server-side encryption. When you upload an object to a bucket for which server-side encryption is enabled, OSS encrypts the object and then stores the encrypted object. When you download the encrypted object, OSS automatically decrypts the object and returns the decrypted object. A header is added to the response to indicate that the object is encrypted on the OSS server.

**Background information**

OSS supports the following encryption methods: SSE-KMS: server-side encryption that uses KMS-managed customer master keys (CMKs) OSS uses the default CMK managed by KMS or a specified CMK to encrypt objects. The CMK is managed by KMS to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability at minimal costs. SSE-OSS: server-side encryption that uses OSS-managed keys OSS uses data keys to encrypt objects and manages the data keys. In addition, OSS uses master keys that are regularly rotated to encrypt data keys. You can enable server-side encryption in the OSS console by using one of the following methods: Method 1: Enable server-side encryption when you create a bucket Method 2: Enable server-side encryption on the Basic Settings tab

**Method 1: Enable server-side encryption when you create a bucket**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click **Create a Bucket**.
3. On the **Create OSS Bucket** page, configure the parameters.
Configure the following parameters to configure server-side encryption for the bucket:
**Server-Side Encryption**: Select an encryption method.
**None**: Server-side encryption is not performed.
**OSS Fully Managed**: Keys managed by OSS are used to encrypt objects in the bucket.
**KMS**: CMKs managed by KMS are used to encrypt objects in the bucket.
**Encryption Algorithm**: Select an encryption algorithm. This parameter is available only when you set the **Server-Side Encryption** parameter to
**OSS Fully Managed** or **KMS**. Valid values:
**AES256**: AES256 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The CMKs used to encrypt the data keys are rotated
regularly.
**SM4**: SM4 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The CMKs used to encrypt the data keys are rotated
regularly.
**AccessKey Pair ID**: This parameter is available only when you select **KMS** for **Server-Side Encryption**. OSS uses the specified CMK to encrypt
objects in the bucket. To select a CMK ID for server-side encryption, you must create the CMK in the KMS console.
4. Click **Submit**.

**Method 2: Enable server-side encryption on the Basic Settings tab**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Server-side encryption** section, click **Settings**.
4. Configure the server-side encryption parameters.
**Server-Side Encryption**: Select an encryption method.
**None**: Server-side encryption is not performed.
**OSS fully managed**: Keys managed by OSS are used to encrypt your data.
**KMS**: CMKs managed by KMS are used to encrypt objects in the bucket.
**Encryption Algorithm**: Select an encryption algorithm. This parameter is available only when you set the **Server-Side Encryption** parameter to
**OSS fully managed** or **KMS**. Valid values:
**AES256**: AES256 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The CMKs used to encrypt the data keys are rotated
regularly.
**SM4**: SM4 is used to encrypt each object in the bucket by using different data keys. The CMKs used to encrypt the data keys are rotated
regularly.
**CMK**: This parameter is available only when you set the **Server-Side Encryption** parameter to **KMS**. OSS uses the specified CMK to encrypt
objects in the bucket. To select a CMK ID for server-side encryption, you must create the CMK in the KMS console.
5. Click **Submit**.

**Important**

The configurations of the default encryption method for a bucket do not affect the encryption configurations of existing objects within the bucket. You can configure static website hosting for your bucket and access this static website by using the bucket endpoint.
1. Log in to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Static page** section, click **Settings**.
4. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Default home page | Specify an index page that functions similarly to index.html. Only HTML objects can be set as the index page. Static website hosting cannot be enabled if no default pages are specified. |
| Default 404 page | Specify the default 404 error page that is returned when the path is incorrect. Only HTML, JPG, PNG, BMP, and WEBP objects under the root directory can be set as the 404 error page. If you do not specify this parameter, the default 404 page is disabled. |

5. Click **Submit**.
You can configure hotlink protection for a bucket in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console to protect your bucket from unauthorized access.

**Background information**

When a browser requests an object from OSS, the Referer header in the HTTP request identifies the URL of the source page. OSS checks the Referer header value to determine the validity of the request source and allows or denies access based on preset rules. Referer whitelist: Only domain names on the whitelist are allowed to access OSS resources. Referer blacklist: Domain names on the blacklist are not allowed to access OSS resources. Empty Referer: If you turn off Empty Referer, only HTTP requests or HTTPS requests that include a trusted Referer field can access objects in the bucket. After you configure a Referer whitelist for a bucket, OSS authenticates requests to objects in the bucket only when the requests are initiated from signed URLs or anonymous users. Requests that contain the Authorization field in the header are not authenticated.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Anti-theft chain** section, click **Settings**.
4. Set the parameters as described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Referer | Configure a Referer whitelist. Click Add Referer and enter a domain name or an IP address. You can use asterisks (*) and question marks (?) as wildcard characters. To add more Referer values, click Add Referer and repeat this step. Examples: If you add www.example.com to the Referer whitelist, requests sent from URLs that start withw ww.example.com, such as www.example.com/123 and www.example.com.cn, are allowed. If you add *www.example.com/ to the Referer whitelist, requests sent fromh ttp://www.example.com/ and https://www.example.com/ are allowed. You can use an asterisk (*) as a wildcard character to represent zero or multiple characters. For example, if you add *.example.com to the Referer whitelist, requests sent from URLs such as help.example.com and www.example.com are allowed. You can use a question mark (?) as a wildcard character to represent a single character. For example, if you add example?.com to the Referer whitelist, requests sent from URLs such as examplea.com and exampleb.com are allowed. You can add domain names or IP addresses that include a port number, such asw ww.example.com:8080 and 10.10.10.10:8080, to the Referer whitelist. |
| Blacklist Referer | Configure a Referer blacklist. Click Add blacklist Referer and enter a domain name or an IP address. You can use asterisks (*) and question marks (?) as wildcard characters. To add more Referer values to the blacklist, click Add blacklist Referer and repeat this step. Examples: If you add www.example.com to the Referer blacklist, requests sent from URLs that start withw ww.example.com, such as www.example.com/123 and www.example.com.cn, are rejected. If you add *www.example.com/ to the Referer blacklist, requests sent fromh ttp://www.example.com/ and https://www.example.com/ are rejected. You can use an asterisk (*) as a wildcard character to represent zero or multiple characters. For example, if you add *.example.com to the Referer blacklist, requests sent from URLs such as help.example.com and www.example.com are rejected. You can use a question mark (?) as a wildcard character to represent a single character. For example, if you add example?.com to the Referer blacklist, requests sent from URLs such as examplea.com and exampleb.com are rejected. You can add domain names or IP addresses that include a port number, such asw ww.example.com:8080 and 10.10.10.10:8080, to the Referer blacklist. |
| Empty Referer | Specifies whether to allow empty Referer fields in requests. An HTTP or HTTPS request with an empty Referer field indicates that the request does not contain the Referer field or the Referer field is empty. If you do not allow empty Referer fields, only HTTP or HTTPS requests that include a trusted Referer field can access objects in the bucket. |

By default, if you use the bucket domain name to preview an MP4 object, the browser sends a request that contains the Referer field and a request that does not contain the Referer field at the same time. Therefore, to allow access to the MP4 object in your bucket, you must not only add the bucket endpoint to the Referer field but also allow empty Referer fields. To preview a non-MP4 object by using the bucket domain name, you only need to allow empty Referer fields.
5. Click **Submit**.
This topic describes how to configure Cross-Origin Requests (CORS) to implement cross-origin access.

**Background information**

Object Storage Service (OSS) supports CORS over HTML5 to implement cross-origin access. When OSS receives a cross-origin request or an OPTIONS request for a bucket, OSS reads the CORS rules of the bucket and checks the relevant permissions. OSS checks the rules in turn. If OSS finds the first match, the corresponding header fields are included in the response. If the request fails to match the CORS rules, OSS does not include CORS headers in the response. You can configure up to 10 CORS rules for a bucket. CORS rules must be unique.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Cross-domain settings** section, click **Settings**.
4. On the page that appears, click **Create a rule**. In the **Create a rule** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Source | Yes | The origins from which cross-origin requests are allowed. When you configure this parameter, take note of the following items: You can specify multiple allowed origins. Separate multiple origins with line feeds. An origin URL must include the protocol, such as HTTP or HTTPS. You can use an asterisk (*) as the wildcard character in an origin URL. Each origin can contain up to one asterisk (*). If an origin URL does not use the default port number, specify the actual port number. Example: https://www.example.com:8080 . The following examples show how to configure allowed origins: To allow requests from a specific origin, specify the origin URL. Example: https://www.example.com . To allow requests from subdomains of a specific root domain, use an asterisk (*) wildcard character in an origin URL. Example: https://*.example.com . To match all domain names, enter only an asterisk (*) as the wildcard character. |
| Allowed Methods | Yes | The methods that cross-origin requests are allowed to use. You can select multiple request methods at the same time. Valid values: GET: obtains files. POST: uploads forms. PUT: uploads objects in simple upload mode. DELETE: deletes files. HEAD: obtains the object metadata. |
| Allowed Headers | No | The response headers of the allowed cross-origin requests. When you configure this parameter, take note of the following items: This parameter is in the key:value format and case-insensitive. Example: content-type:text/plain . You can configure multiple response headers. Separate multiple response headers with line feeds. Each header can contain up to one asterisk (*) wildcard character. Set this parameter to an asterisk (*) wildcard character if you do not have special requirements. |
| Exposed Headers | No | The response headers of allowed access requests from applications, such as an XMLHttpRequest object in JavaScript. Exposed headers cannot contain asterisk (*) wildcard characters. |
| Cache Timeout (Seconds) | No | The timeout period of the response that is cached by the browser for an OPTIONS preflight request destined for specific resources. Unit: seconds. |

5. Click **OK**.
You can configure lifecycle rules to regularly delete expired objects and fragments to reduce storage costs.

**Prerequisites**

An OSS bucket is created. For more information, see Create buckets. Take note of the following items when you configure lifecycle rules for a bucket: After a lifecycle rule is configured, it is loaded within 24 hours and takes effect within 24 hours after it is loaded. Check the configurations of a rule before you save the rule. Objects that are deleted based on lifecycle rules cannot be recovered. Configure lifecycle rules based on your business requirements. You can configure up to 100 lifecycle rules for a bucket in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console. To configure more rules, use OSS SDKs.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Lifecycle** section, click **Settings**.
4. On the page that appears, click **Create a rule**. In the **Create a lifecycle** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the
parameters. Parameters for buckets for which the versioning feature is disabled

|   | Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|   |   | Status | Enable or disable the lifecycle rule. Valid values: Enable and Disable. |

| Clo | ud Defined Storag | e User Guide·OSS |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   | Basic Settings |   |   |   |
|   |   | Strategy | Select the objects to which the lifecycle rule applies. You can selectM atch by prefix or Match to the entire Bucket. Note If you select Match by prefix, you can configure different lifecycle rules for objects whose names contain different prefixes. If you select Match to the entire Bucket, only one lifecycle rule can be configured for the bucket. |   |
|   |   | Prefix | If you set the Strategy parameter to Match by prefix, you must specify the prefix of the objects to which the rule applies. For example, if you want the rule to apply to objects whose names start with img, enter img . |   |
|   |   | Label | If you turn on Label, click Add Tags and configure tags to apply the rule to objects that have the specified tags. For example, if you select Match by prefix and set Prefix to img, Key to a, and Value to 1, the rule applies to all objects that contain the img prefix in their names and have the a=1 tag. |   |
|   | Clear Policy | File time policy | Important You must configure at least one of the File time policy and Fragment expiration policy parameters for each lifecycle rule. Deleted objects cannot be recovered. Proceed with caution. Specify an object expiration policy. You can select Specify the number of days, Specified date, or Not enabled. If you select Not enabled, this parameter does not take effect. |   |
|   |   | Delete a file | Specify when objects expire based on Specify the number of days or Specified date that you set for File time policy. After objects expire, they are deleted. Specify the number of days: Specify the number of days to retain objects after they are last modified. Select the check box next to Delete a file and specify a number such as N. The objects expire N days after they are last modified. Then, the objects are deleted the next day after they expire. For example, if you specify the number as 30, objects that are last modified on January 1, 2019 are deleted on February 1, 2019. Specified date: Specify the expiration date. Select the check box next to Delete a file and specify an expiration date. The objects that are last modified before this date expire and are deleted. For example, if you set Expiration Date to January 1, 2019, objects that are last modified before January 1, 2019 are deleted. |   |

Deleted fragments cannot be recovered. Proceed with caution. If you turn on Label in the Basic Settings section, the Fragment expiration policy parameter is unavailable. Specify the operation that you want to perform on expired fragments. You can selectS pecify the number of days, Specified date, or Not enabled. If you select Not enabled, the Fragment expiration policy parameter does not take effect. |   |
|   |   | Delete fragments | Specify when fragments expire based on Specify the number of days or Specified date that you set for Fragment expiration policy. After fragments expire, they are deleted. |   |

Parameters for buckets for which the versioning feature is enabled Configure the parameters in the **Basic Settings** and **Clean up debris** sections in the same way as the parameters that you configure for buckets for which the versioning feature is disabled. The following table describes only the parameters that are different from the parameters that you configure for buckets for which the versioning feature is disabled.

|   | Section | Parameter | Description |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   | Current Version | Removal of Delete Marker | After you enable versioning for the bucket, the Removal of Delete Marker option is added to the Object Lifecycle parameter. Other parameters are the same as those you can configure for buckets that have versioning disabled. If you select Removal of Delete Marker, and an object has only one version, which is also a delete marker, OSS considers the delete marker expired and removes the delete marker. If an object has multiple versions and the current version of the object is a delete marker, OSS retains the delete marker. |   |
|   |   | Object Lifecycle | Specify the time when previous versions expire. You can select Validity Period (Days) or Disabled. If you select Disabled, the Object Lifecycle parameter does not take effect. |   |

|   | r Guide·OSS |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
|   | Previous Versions |   |   |
|   |   | Delete | Specify when objects expire based on Specify the number of days that you set for File time policy. After objects expire, they are deleted. Select the Delete a file check box and specify the number of days that objects can be retained as previous versions. The previous versions are deleted one day after they expire. Important If the current version of an object is deleted based on a lifecycle rule, OSS does not delete the current version but converts the current version to a previous version and adds a delete marker to the object. The delete marker becomes the current version of the object. If a previous version of an object is deleted based on a lifecycle rule, OSS deletes the previous version. If you configure a lifecycle rule to delete previous versions, delete markers that are stored as previous versions are also deleted. |

5. Click **OK**.

**What to do next**
