You can use bucket tags to classify and manage buckets. For example, you can list buckets that have specific tags and configure access control lists (ACLs) for buckets that have specific tags.

**Background information**

The bucket tagging feature uses a key-value pair to identify a bucket. You can add tags to buckets that are used for different purposes and manage the buckets by tags. Only the bucket owner or authorized Resource Access Management (RAM) users can configure tags for the bucket. Otherwise, 403 Forbidden is returned with the error code AccessDenied. A tag is a key-value pair. You can configure up to 20 tags for a bucket. The key can be up to 64 characters in length, and cannot start with `http://` , `https://` , or `Aliyun` . The key cannot be left empty. The value can be up to 128 characters in length, and can be left empty. The key and value of a tag must be encoded in UTF-8.
1. Log in to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Bucket label** section, click **Settings**.
By default, each bucket has a system tag. You cannot modify or delete the system tag.
4. Click **Add entry**. In the line that appears, configure the **key** and **value** parameters to add a tag.
To add multiple tags, click **Add entry** and repeat this step. To delete a custom tag, click the icon to the right of the tag.
5. Click **Submit**.
If the capacity of a bucket reaches the specified storage quota, write operations such as PutObject, MultipartUpload, CopyObject, PostObject, and AppendObject cannot be performed on the bucket. This topic describes how to configure the storage quota of a bucket in Object Storage Service (OSS). Take note of the following items when you configure the storage quota of a bucket: Before you configure the storage quota of a bucket, make sure that the quota does not limit your business because write operations cannot be performed if the bucket capacity reaches the quota. In most cases, it takes about 1 hour for OSS to determine whether the bucket capacity exceeds the storage quota. In some cases, it can take longer than 1 hour.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Set capacity threshold** section, click **Settings**.
You can view the storage quota of the bucket in this section.
4. On the **Modify OSS Bucket** page, select a unit and drag the slider to adjust the quota or enter a quota value.
Supported units: TiB and GiB. Valid values if you select TiB: 1 to 2000000. Valid values if you select GiB: 1 to 2048000000.
5. Click **Submit**.
After you submit the request, you can click **OK** in the message that appears to return to the **Overview** tab.
6. View the storage quota of the bucket.
i. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket whose quota you want to view. ii. On the **Overview** tab, find the **Basic settings** section. iii. View the storage quota of the bucket. The storage quota of the bucket is displayed in the **Basic settings** section. Example: A storage quota of 2 TiB is configured for the bucket. Ensure that the quota is larger than the storage usage that you require. Cross-region replication (CRR) automatically and asynchronously replicates objects between Object Storage Service (OSS) buckets in different regions. CRR synchronizes object modifications in near real time, including creation, overwriting, and deletion, from a source bucket to a destination bucket.

**Prerequisites**

The source and destination buckets are created. For more information, see Create buckets.

**Background information**

CRR helps you meet compliance requirements for cross-region disaster recovery and data replication. Objects in the destination bucket are exact replicas of those in the source bucket. They share the same object name, content, and metadata, such as creation time, owner, user-defined metadata, and access control lists (ACLs).
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, find the bucket that you want to manage and click its name.
3. On the bucket details page, click the **Basic settings** tab. On the Basic settings tab, find the **Cross-region replication** section and click **Enable**
**synchronization**.
4. In the **Cross-region replication** panel, configure a CRR rule.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| SOURCE Bucket region | The region in which the current bucket is located. |
| SOURCE Bucket | The name of the current bucket. |
| Target region | The region in which the destination bucket is located. The source and destination buckets for CRR must be located in different regions. You cannot replicate data between buckets in the same region. |
| Target Bucket | The destination bucket to which you want to replicate data. The source and destination buckets in a CRR rule cannot be specified in other CRR rules. For example, if you configure a CRR rule to replicate data from Bucket A to Bucket B, Bucket A and Bucket B cannot be specified in other CRR rules. |
| Data Synchronization object | The objects that you want to replicate to the destination bucket. Valid values: Synchronize all files: All objects in the source bucket are replicated to the destination bucket. Specify the file name prefix for synchronization: Only objects whose names match one of the specified prefixes are replicated to the destination bucket. For example, if you have a folder named management in the root folder of the source bucket and want to replicate objects in a subfolder named abc in management, you can specify the prefix management/abc/ . You can specify up to 10 prefixes. |
| Data Synchronization policy | The operations that you want to replicate. Valid values: Add/change synchronization: OSS replicates only object creation and update operations from the source bucket to the destination bucket. Add/delete/change synchronization: OSS replicates object creation, update, and deletion operations from the source bucket to the destination bucket. |

| Synchronize historical data | Specifies whether to replicate historical data (data that exists in the source bucket before you enable CRR) to the destination bucket. Valid values: Synchronization: OSS replicates historical data to the destination bucket. Important When historical data is replicated, objects that are replicated from the source bucket may overwrite objects that have the same names in the destination bucket. To prevent data loss, we recommend that you enable versioning for the source and destination buckets. Out of Sync: OSS replicates only objects that are uploaded or updated after CRR is enabled to the destination bucket. |
|---|---|
| KMS encrypts target objects | By default, objects that are encrypted by using customer master keys (CMKs) managed by Key Management Service (KMS) in the source bucket cannot be synchronized to the destination bucket even if CRR is enabled. To replicate objects encrypted by using CMKs managed by KMS to the destination bucket, you must create a Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has permissions to manage and decrypt the objects by using CMKs and attach the role to your account or RAM user. This parameter is required only if you configure the Target region parameter. Note If you specify a CMK ID to encrypt objects when you create a bucket or upload objects, turn on this switch. |
| KMS key used | The KMS-managed CMK for object encryption and decryption. This parameter is required only if you turn onK MS encrypts target objects. Make sure that you have created a KMS CMK in the KMS console. |
| Authorization role | The role attached to the OSS service. The linked role must have permissions to perform operations on encrypted objects and encrypt and decrypt objects by using KMS-managed CMKs. This parameter is required only if you turn on KMS encrypts target objects. To attach a role that has the required permissions, you can use the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole or create a custom role. For more information about how to grant permissions to a role, see Grants permissions to a role. Use the predefined RAM role OSS provides the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole. You can use this predefined role when you configure a RAM role during bucket creation. Create a custom role You can click Create Role to create a custom role. |

5. Click **OK**.
After a CRR rule is configured, the replication task starts in 3 to 5 minutes. Then, you can view the replication progress. In CRR, data is asynchronously replicated in near real time. The period of time that is required to replicate data from the source bucket to the destination bucket may range from a few minutes to a few hours, depending on the data size. If you want to replicate an object encrypted based on KMS from the source bucket to the destination bucket, KMS must be configured for the destination bucket. Otherwise, data replication fails. You can use the cross-cloud replication feature to synchronize Object Storage Service (OSS) data between two clouds. This topic describes how to configure cross-cloud replication. In cross-cloud replication scenarios, the versioning states of the source and destination buckets in OSS must be consistent to ensure data consistency and operating system compatibility. That is, both the source and destination buckets must have the versioning feature enabled and be in the same state, but cannot be in the Versioning Disabled or Versioning Paused state. If the source or destination site is a zone-disaster recovery site, the disaster recovery failover feature cannot work as expected after cross-cloud replication is enabled. In this case, we recommend that you use Apsara Stack Resilience for Disaster Recovery (ASR-DR) for geo-disaster recovery. You cannot use a specific CMK ID to encrypt objects when you create a bucket or upload objects for cross-cloud replication.

Zone-disaster recovery synchronizes objects in a bucket to a secondary bucket with the same name as the bucket in the secondary cluster to enable cluster-level disaster recovery. If zone-disaster recovery is enabled, a secondary bucket with the same name as the primary bucket is automatically created and objects in the primary bucket are automatically synchronized to the secondary bucket. By default, cluster-disaster recovery is enabled for buckets that are created by using the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.

**Background information**

By default, objects that are encrypted by using customer master keys (CMKs) managed by Key Management Service (KMS) in the source bucket cannot be synchronized to the destination bucket even if zone-disaster recovery is enabled. To synchronize objects encrypted by using CMKs managed by KMS to the destination bucket, you must create a Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has permissions to manage and decrypt the objects by using CMKs and attach the role to your account or RAM user. For more information, see Grant permissions to a role.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Disaster recovery in the same city** section, click **Settings**.
4. Perform operations as needed.
To synchronize objects encrypted by using CMKs managed by KMS to the destination bucket, turn on **Enable local disaster recovery mode**, select **KMS-Encrypted Object**, and then specify a CMK ID and a RAM role. The following table describes the **KMS Key Used** and **RAM Role**
**Authorization** parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| KMS Key Used | Select a KMS-managed CMK for object encryption and decryption. This parameter is available only whenK MS-based Encryption is turned on. Make sure that you have created a KMS CMK in the KMS console. |
| RAM Role Authorization | Attach a role to the OSS service. The role must have permissions to perform operations on encrypted objects and encrypt and decrypt objects by using KMS-managed CMKs. This parameter is available only when KMS-based Encryption is turned on. To attach a role that has the required permissions, you can use the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole or create a custom role. For more information about how to grant permissions to a role, see Grants permissions to a role. Use the predefined RAM role OSS provides the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole. You can use this predefined role when you configure a RAM role during bucket creation. Create a custom role You can click Create Role to create a custom role. |

To disable zone-disaster recovery, turn off **Enable local disaster recovery mode**.
5. Click **Submit**.
After you upload objects to a bucket, Object Storage Service (OSS) automatically generates URLs for the uploaded objects. You can use these URLs to access the objects. If you want to access the objects by using a custom domain name, you must map the custom domain name to the bucket in which the objects are stored.

**Important**

Before you map a custom domain name, make sure that you have an available domain name. If the bucket mapped to the domain name is deployed in the Chinese mainland and serves Internet users, you must complete an ICP filing for the domain name.

**Background information**

Mapping a custom domain name to an OSS bucket is achieved using a canonical name (CNAME) record in Domain Name System (DNS). A CNAME record maps your custom domain name to the access endpoint of the bucket. When a user visits the custom domain name, the DNS system resolves the request to the corresponding OSS bucket endpoint, enabling direct access to the OSS resources. You can map multiple custom domain names to a bucket. A domain name can be mapped to only one bucket.

**Step 1: Map a custom domain name**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, find the bucket that you want to manage and click its name.
3. On the bucket details page, click the **Basic settings** tab. On the Basic settings tab, find the **Domain name management** section and click
**Settings**.
4. On the page that appears, click **Bind Domain name**.
5. In the **Bind Domain name** panel, enter a domain name and click **OK**.
To unmap a custom domain name from a bucket, find it and click **Unbind** in the **Operation** column.

**Step 2: Resolve the custom domain name to an OSS endpoint**

After the custom domain name is mapped to the bucket, the custom domain name does not take effect immediately. To make the custom domain name take effect, you must configure a CNAME record to point the custom domain name to the endpoint of the OSS bucket.

**Important**

Before you configure the CNAME record, make sure that the custom domain name is mapped to the OSS bucket in the OSS console. Otherwise, the OSS bucket fails to be identified when you use the custom domain name to access OSS. As a result, unexpected content is returned. After you unmap the custom domain name from the OSS bucket, you must also delete the corresponding CNAME record.
1. Obtain the endpoint of the OSS bucket.
i. Log in to the OSS console. ii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, find the bucket that you want to manage and click its name. iii. On the bucket details page, click the **Overview** tab. On the Overview tab, find the **Access domain name** section and copy the endpoint of the OSS bucket. If you access OSS over the Internet only, copy the **endpoint of the OSS bucket** in the **Internet access** row. If you access OSS over an internal network only, copy the **endpoint of the OSS bucket** in the **Intranet access** row.
2. Configure a CNAME record based on the client access source.
If the access sources include both the Internet and an internal network, complex network routing and DNS configurations are involved. We recommend that you contact Apsara Stack technical support to help evaluate your architecture solution and provide professional configuration guidance.

**Access from the Internet only**

The following example uses Alibaba Cloud DNS to describe how to configure a CNAME record.

**Important**

Configuration methods may vary for other DNS providers. The actual platform operations prevail. If a domain name belongs to another Alibaba Cloud account or another DNS provider, you must configure a CNAME record at the corresponding DNS provider. i. Log in to the Alibaba Cloud DNS console with the Alibaba Cloud account to which the domain name belongs. Find the domain name that you want to manage and click **Settings** in the Actions column. ii. On the page that appears, click **Add Record**. In the dialog box that appears, configure the parameters that are described in the following table. You can use the default settings for other parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Record Type | The type of the record. In this example, CNAME is used. |
| Hostname | The hostname. If the primary domain name is mapped, set this parameter to @ . If a subdomain name is mapped, enter the prefix of the subdomain name. For example, if the subdomain named image.oss-example.cn is mapped, set this parameter to image . |
| Record Values | The public endpoint of the OSS bucket. Example: pub******.oss-cn-******.******.com . |

iii. Click **OK**. In the **Change Resource Record Confirmation** dialog box, click **OK**.

**Access from an internal network only**

We recommend that your system administrator add a CNAME record for the custom domain name on the internal DNS server of your enterprise. The CNAME record points the custom domain name to the internal endpoint of the OSS bucket. Also, make sure that the valid internal DNS server address is configured for all client devices. Configuration methods differ for various DNS servers, such as Windows DNS and BIND9 servers. For more information, see the official configuration manual for your specific platform. When you configure the CNAME record, make sure that the internal endpoint of the OSS bucket is used as the destination address of the CNAME record.

**Important**

DNS changes may take several minutes to hours to propagate, depending on the time-to-live (TTL) setting of the CNAME record. It is normal for access to fail immediately after configuration. Wait or try clearing your local DNS cache.

| Cl | oud Defined Storage User Guide·OSS |
|---|---|

**Step 3: Verify whether the custom domain name can be used to access OSS**

You can use the HTTP protocol to verify whether the custom domain name can be used to access objects in the OSS bucket. After the custom domain name is mapped and the CNAME record is configured, you can select a verification method based on the access control list (ACL) settings of the OSS bucket. Before you access objects in an OSS bucket over HTTPS, enable HTTPS access. For more information, see the Enable HTTPS access section of this topic.

**Public-read or public-read-write buckets**

Enter `http://your_domain_name/object_path` in your browser to access an object in the OSS bucket. The `your_domain_name` parameter specifies the mapped custom domain name. The `object_path` parameter specifies the path of the object in the OSS bucket. For example, if the object named `dest.jpg` is stored in the `exampledir` directory of the OSS bucket, the value of the `object_path` parameter is `exampledir/dest.jpg` .

**Private buckets**

Accessing objects in a private bucket requires a signed URL. The following section describes how to obtain the signed URL of an object in the OSS console.
1. Obtain an object URL. For more information, see Obtain object URLs.
2. Replace the endpoint of the bucket in the object URL with the custom domain name that is mapped to the bucket. Then, enter the object URL in your
browser to access the object.

**(Optional) Enable HTTPS access**

To implement data encryption in transit and identity verification and ensure access security, you can enable secure HTTPS access for the custom domain name that is mapped to the OSS bucket.

**Step 1: Prepare a certificate**

To prepare a certificate, you must first create a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) file for the custom domain name and download the CSR file in the Certificate Management Service console. Then, use the CSR file to apply for a certificate. Finally, upload the created certificate to the Certificate Management Service console.
1. Create a CSR file for the custom domain name mapped to the bucket and download the CSR file.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Security** > **Certificate Management Service**. iii. On the **SSL Certificate Management** page, click the **CSR Management** tab. iv. On the **CSR Management** tab, click **Create CSR**. v. On the **Create CSR** page, configure the parameters in the Region Information, Basic Information, and Subject Information sections. Then, click
**Submit**.

| Parameter |   | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Region Information | Organization | test | The organization and resource set to which the CSR file belongs and the region in which the CSR file is deployed. The organization, resource set, and region of the CSR file are the same as those of the bucket. |
|   | Resource Set | ResourceSet(test) |   |
|   | Region | cn-beijing-env1-d01 |   |
| Basic Information | Name | mytest | The name of the CSR file. |
|   | CN | osstest | The certificate identifier. You can set this parameter to the primary domain name of the service being secured, or a custom string. Important Modern browsers and operating systems have deprecated the use of the Common Name (CN) field for domain validation. In accordance with standards such as RFC 6125 (2011), you must list all valid domain names to be secured by this certificate in the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field. Specify all valid domain names in the SAN field. |
|   | SAN | exampledoc.com | The custom domain name that is mapped to the OSS bucket. If you want to specify multiple domain names, separate them with commas (,). |
|   | Key Algorithm | RSA | The key algorithm and strength of the certificate. |
|   | Key Strength | 2048 |   |
| Subject Information | Country Code (C) | CN | The two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. |
|   | Province (ST) | Beijing | The full name of the province. |
|   | City (L) | Beijing | The full name of the city. |

On the **Upload Certificate** tab, click **Upload Certificate**. iii. 5. In the **Certificate hosting** panel, select a certificate name and click **OK**.

**Important**

Make sure that the SAN field of the selected certificate contains the destination domain name and the certificate is within the validity period. Otherwise, an error is reported. After the certificate is hosted, find it and click **Details** in the **HTTPS certificate** column to view the details of the certificate. The details include the certificate name, ID, and status.

**Step 3: Verify HTTPS access**

After the certificate hosting configuration is complete, wait for it to take effect. Then, enter the URL of an object in your browser to verify whether HTTPS encryption works as expected. If yes, data transmission security is ensured.
1. Turn on **Use HTTPS** when you obtain an object URL.
2. Replace the endpoint of the bucket in the object URL with the custom domain name that is mapped to the bucket. Then, enter the object URL in your
browser to access the object. Communication between client applications and Object Storage Service (OSS) is encrypted by using the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. TLS is a standard cryptographic protocol that ensures privacy and data integrity between clients and servers that communicate over the Internet. After you configure the TLS version and the cipher suite on an OSS client, the client can use only the configured TLS version to send requests to and receive requests from OSS to ensure communication security.

**TLS versions**

The TLS protocol supports the following versions: TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, TLS 1.2, and TLS 1.3. OSS supports only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The following table describes the applicable scenarios of each version and the mainstream browsers that support each version.

| Protocol version | Description | Applicable scenario | Supported browser |
|---|---|---|---|
| TLS 1.2 | TLS 1.2 further enhances security for network connections, and launches new features, such as Server Name Indication (SNI) and handshake protocols. TLS 1.2 supports more encryption algorithms, including AES-GCM, AES-CBC, and ECDHE. | TLS 1.2 is suitable for most common secure communication scenarios, including web applications, e-commerce websites, emails, and virtual private networks (VPNs). | IE11+ Chrome 30+ Firefox 27+ Safri 7+ |
| TLS 1.3 | TLS 1.3 significantly improves security, performance, and privacy. TLS 1.3 no longer supports some insecure encryption algorithms. It supports more powerful key exchange algorithms and encryption algorithms that reduce the delay of the handshake process, and also provides better forward secrecy and authentication mechanisms. | TLS 1.3 is suitable for scenarios in which high security, better performance, and privacy protection are required, such as in financial institutions, large Internet companies, and government agencies. | Chrome 70+ Firefox 63+ |

If you disable TLS version management, TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are supported by default. If you enable TLS version management, you can select TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. Downgrading the TLS version, such as changing the TLS version from TLS 1.3 to TLS 1.2, or disabling TLS version management may cause security and compliance issues. Proceed with caution when you perform the operation. Before you disable a TLS version, make sure that it is not the only version used by clients. You can set the TLS version by using OSS SDK for Java.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **TLS Version Management** section, click **Settings**.
4. Turn on **TLS Version Management**, and select an allowed TLS version.
5. Click **Save**.
After you specify a TLS version, the clients can use only the TLS version to send requests to and receive requests from OSS. This improves communication security. If you access data in an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket for which no back-to-origin rule is configured and the data does not exist, 404 Not Found is returned. However, if you configure back-to-origin rules that contain the correct origin URLs, you can obtain the data from the origin based on the back-to-origin rules.

**Background information**

You can configure mirroring-based or redirection-based back-to-origin rules for hot migration and specific request redirection. Mirroring-based back-to-origin After mirroring-based back-to-origin rules are configured for a bucket, you can obtain an object in the bucket based on the rules when the requested object is not found. For example, when you perform the GetObject operation on an object and the object is not found, OSS retrieves the object based on the origin URL, returns the object, and then writes the object to OSS. Mirroring-based back-to-origin rules are used to seamlessly migrate data to OSS. This feature allows you to migrate a service that already runs on a user-created origin or in another cloud service to OSS without interrupting services. Redirection-based back-to-origin After redirection-based back-to-origin rules are configured for a bucket, you can obtain an object in the bucket based on the rules when the requested object is not found. For example, when you perform the GetObject operation on an object and the object is not found, OSS redirects the request to the origin URL, and then a browser or client returns the content from the origin. You can use this feature to redirect requests for objects and develop various business applications based on redirection. You can configure up to 20 back-to-origin rules for a single bucket. Configured rules are run in a sequence in which they are configured. To configure back-to-origin rules, you must set the access control list (ACL) of the bucket to public-read. Buckets whose ACL is set to private do not support the back-to-origin feature. Objects with source image protection enabled do not support the back-to-origin feature.

**Configure a mirroring-based back-to-origin rule**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to configure a mirroring-
based back-to-origin rule.
3. Click the **Basic settings** tab. In the **Mirroring back to source** section, click **Settings**.
4. Click **Create a rule**. In the **Create a rule** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Yes | Select Mirroring. In this mode, when a requested object cannot be found in OSS, OSS automatically retrieves the object from the origin, stores the object in OSS, and then returns the content to the requester. |
| Condition | Yes | Configure the conditions that trigger the back-to-origin rule. A rule is triggered only when all conditions are met. HTTP Status Code: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the specified HTTP status code is returned. The default HTTP status code is 404, which indicates that the rule is triggered when the requested object is not found in OSS and HTTP status code 404 is returned. By default, this option is selected when you select the Mirroring method. Object Name Prefix: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the name of the requested object contains the specified prefix. For example, when this parameter is set to abc/, the back-to-origin rule is triggered when you access https://bucketname.endpoint/abc/image.jpg . File Name Suffix: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the name of the requested object contains the specified suffix. For example, when this parameter is set to .jpg, the back-to-origin rule is triggered when you access https://bucketname.endpoint/image.jpg . Note If you configure only one mirroring-based back-to-origin rule for the bucket, you can leave the Object Name Prefix parameter and the File Name Suffix parameter empty. If you configure multiple mirroring-based back-to-origin rules for the bucket, you must specify different name prefixes or suffixes to differentiate back-to-origin rules. |
| Replace or Delete File Prefix | No | You can configure this parameter after you select and configure Object Name Prefix. When OSS sends a request to the origin, the content of Object Name Prefix is replaced with that of Replace or Delete File Prefix . Example: You want to store the object obtained from the origin in them irror folder under the root folder of the bucket. If the name of the requested object is path/test/photo.jpg, set File Name Prefix to mirror/ , Replace or Delete File Prefix to test/ , and the third column of Origin URL to path . In this case, when you access https://bucketname.endpoint/mirror/photo.jpg , if photo.jpg does not exist, OSS sends the https://Origin URL/path/test/photo.jpg request to obtain this object. If the object is obtained from the origin, OSS stores this object in the mirror/ folder and returns the object to you. |
| Origin URL | Yes | Configure the information about the origin URL. First column: Select HTTP or HTTPS based on the protocol used by the origin. Note If Server Name Indication (SNI) is enabled on the origin, HTTPS that you select does not take effect. Second column: Enter the endpoint or IP address of the origin. Internal endpoints and IP addresses are not supported. If you enter an IP address, ensure that the origin corresponding to the IP address can be accessed by using the IP address. Third column: Enter the folder where the requested object is stored. Separate subfolders in a folder with forward slashes (/). Example: abc/123 . |
| MD5 Verification | No | If this option is selected, the MD5 hash of the object obtained from the origin is checked. When the response contains the Content-MD5 header value, OSS calculates the MD5 hash of the object and checks whether the MD5 hash of the object matches the Content-MD5 header value. If the MD5 hash of the object matches the Content-MD5 header value, the client obtains the object, and OSS saves the object by using the mirroring-based back-to-origin rule. If the MD5 hash of the object does not match the Content-MD5 header value, the client can obtain the object as the file is already passed to the client. However, OSS does not save the object. This is because OSS calculates the MD5 hash of the object to check whether the object is damaged or tampered. The mismatch indicates that the object is damaged or tampered. |
| Keep Forward Slash in Origin URL | No | OSS does not support object names that start with a forward slash (/). Therefore, if the name of the requested object starts with a forward slash (/), you must select this option to obtain the requested object based on the back- to-origin rules. For example, the origin is https://www.example.com , the name of the requested object is /object.txt, and the name of the bucket is examplebucket. If this option is selected, the default public endpoint to access the requested object is https://examplebucket.endpoint//object.txt , and the origin URL is https://www.example.com//object.txt . The object is obtained from OSS, returned to the client, and then saved in the bucket as object.txt. |
| Origin Parameter | No | If this option is selected, the query string included in the request to OSS is transferred to the origin. |
| 3xx Response | No | If this option is selected, OSS follows the origin to direct the request to obtain the resource and stores the resource in buckets. If this option is not selected, OSS passes the 3xx response without obtaining the resource. |
| Set Transmission Rule of HTTP Header | No | You can configure the transmission rule for HTTP headers to customize transmission actions such as passthrough, filtering, or modification. For more information, see the following examples of transmission rule configurations for HTTP headers. |

The following figure provides a sample transmission rule for HTTP headers. Assume that you send a request that contains the following HTTP headers to OSS.

```
GET /object host : bucket.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com aaa-header : aaa bbb-header : bbb ccc-header : 111
```

After the mirroring-based back-to-origin rule is triggered, OSS sends the following request to the origin:

```
GET /object host : source.com aaa-header : aaa ccc-header : ccc
```

Transmission rules do not support the following HTTP headers: Headers that contain the following prefixes: x-ossossx-drs- All standard HTTP headers. Examples: content-length authorization2 authorization range date
5. Click **OK**.

**Configure a redirection-based back-to-origin rule**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to configure a redirection-
based back-to-origin rule.
3. Click the **Basic Settings** tab. In the **Mirroring-based Back-to-origin** section, click **Settings**.
4. Click **Create a rule**. In the **Create a rule** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Yes | Select Redirection. In this mode, OSS redirects requests that meet the conditions to the origin URL over HTTP, and then a browser or client returns the content from the origin to the requester. |

| Condition | Yes | Configure the conditions that trigger the back-to-origin rule. A rule is triggered only when all conditions are met. HTTP Status Code: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the specified HTTP status code is returned. The default HTTP status code is 404, which indicates that the rule is triggered when the requested object is not found in OSS and HTTP status code 404 is returned. Object Name Prefix: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the name of the requested object contains the specified prefix. For example, when this parameter is set to abc/, the back-to-origin rule is triggered when you access https://bucketname.endpoint/abc/image.jpg . File Name Suffix: The back-to-origin rule is triggered when the name of the requested object contains the specified suffix. For example, when this parameter is set to .jpg, the back-to-origin rule is triggered when you access https://bucketname.endpoint/image.jpg . Note If you configure only one redirection-based back-to-origin rule for the bucket, you can leave the Object Name Prefix parameter and the File Name Suffix parameter empty. If you configure multiple redirection-based back-to-origin rules for the bucket, you must specify different name prefixes or suffixes to differentiate back-to-origin rules. |
|---|---|---|
| Replace or Delete File Prefix | No | You can configure this parameter after you select and configure Object Name Prefix. When OSS sends a request to the origin, the content of Object Name Prefix is replaced with that of Replace Object Name Prefix. Note If you select this option, you must set Origin URL to Replace Object Name Prefix. If you set Origin URL to Add Prefix or Suffix or Redirect to Fixed URL, the object name prefix cannot be replaced or deleted. |
| Origin URL | Yes | Configure the information about the origin URL. You must configure the back-to-origin rule based on the origin URL. Configuring the origin URL in accordance with the following rules: First column: Select HTTP or HTTPS based on the protocol used by the origin. Second column: Enter the endpoint or IP address of the origin. Note You can enter IP addresses only when the origin can be directly accessed by using IP addresses. Third column: Configure the redirection-based back-to-origin rule based on the prefix and suffix configurations. Add Prefix or Suffix: Add a prefix or suffix to the redirected URL. The prefix is configured in the third column. The suffix is configured in the fourth column. You can select this option to configure information for the redirected URL when the URL of the requested data excludes a prefix or suffix. For example, the prefix is set to 123/, and the suffix is set to. jpg. When you access https://bucketname.endpoint/image , the request is redirected to https://Origin URL/123/image.jpg . Jump to a fixed address: Access to the requested object is redirected to a specific object. The object address is specified in the third column. Example: abc/myphoto.jpg . Note You can also set the value of this parameter to the URL of a website. For example, if you set the URL to https://www.aliyun.com/index.html , access to the bucket is redirected to the Alibaba Cloud homepage. Replace Object Name Prefix: If you set this parameter and Object Name Prefix for Condition, the prefix in the name of the object to which the access is redirected is replaced with that of the third column. If you set this parameter without setting Object Name Prefix for Condition, the specified prefix is added to the name of the object to which the access is redirected. Separate subfolders in a folder with forward slashes (/). The folder name must end with a forward slash (/) and cannot contain asterisks (*). |
| Origin Parameter | No | If this option is selected, the query string included in the request to OSS is transferred to the origin. |
| Redirection Code | Yes | Select a redirection code from the drop-down list. |

|   | URL/123/image.jpg |
|---|---|

5. Click **OK**.

**Related operations**

After a back-to-origin rule is created, you can modify or delete the back-to-origin rule based on your business requirements.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| Modify a back-to-origin rule | You can modify the Method, Condition, and Origin URL parameters of a back-to-origin rule. 1. Find the back-to-origin rule that you want to modify and clickE dit in the Actions column. 2. In the dialog box that appears, modify the parameters. 3. Click OK. |

| Delete a back-to-origin rule | Find the rule that you want to delete and clickD elete in the Operation column. In the message that appears, click OK. Important After a back-to-origin rule is deleted, if the requested object does not exist, OSS no longer automatically retrieves resources from or redirects requests to the origin, which may cause access failures. Make sure that all data has been synchronized and your business has no dependencies on the bucket associated with the back-to-origin rule that you want to delete, and then delete the back-to-origin rule during off-peak hours. Proceed with caution. A deleted back-to-origin rule cannot be recovered. We recommend that you back up the back-to-origin rule before you delete it. |
|---|---|

Object Storage Service (OSS) allows you to configure a write once read many (WORM) policy for a bucket. During the retention period specified in the policy, you can upload objects to the bucket and access the objects in the bucket but cannot delete or modify the objects in the bucket. You can configure retention policies only for buckets in OSS. You cannot enable versioning and configure retention policies for a bucket at the same time. If versioning is enabled for a bucket, you cannot configure retention policies for the bucket.

**Prerequisites**

An OSS bucket is created. For more information, see Create buckets.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to configure retention policies.
3. Create a retention policy.
i. On the page that appears, click the **Basic Settings** tab. In the **Retention Policy** section, click **Settings**. ii. Click **Create Policy**. iii. In the **Create Policy** panel, configure the **Retention Period** parameter and click **OK**. Valid values: 1 to 25550. Unit: Days. If an existing locked retention policy does not meet your business requirements, you can delete it. Find the locked retention policy that you want to delete, and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
4. Lock the retention policy.

**Important**

If a retention policy is not locked within 24 hours after it is created, the retention policy becomes invalid. After a retention policy is locked, you cannot shorten the retention period or delete the retention policy. You cannot modify or delete data in the bucket during the retention period. i. Click **Lock** in the **Actions** column of the retention policy. ii. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
5. Optional. After the retention policy is locked, you can extend the retention period based on your business requirements.
i. Click **Edit** in the **Actions** column of the retention policy. ii. In the **Edit** panel, configure the **Retention Period** parameter and click **OK**.

**Important**

The new retention period you specify cannot be shorter than the original retention period. After the retention policy is locked, its retention period cannot be shortened. You can configure bucket policies based on your business requirements in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Basic Settings** tab and find the **Bucket Policy** section.
4. Click **Settings**.
5. On the **GUI** tab of the page that appears, click **Authorize**.
You can also configure the policy syntax on the **Syntax** tab.
6. In the **Authorize** panel, configure the parameters and click **OK**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Applied To | Select the resources on which you want to grant other users the access permissions. Whole Bucket: The bucket policy applies to all resources in the bucket. Specific Resources: The bucket policy applies only to specific resources in the bucket. You can configure multiple bucket policies for specific resources in a bucket. Directory-level authorization To configure a bucket policy to grant users the permissions to access all subdirectories and objects in a directory, add an asterisk (*) after the directory name. For example, to grant users the permissions to access all subdirectories and objects in a directory named abc, enter abc/* . Object-level authorization To configure a bucket policy to grant users the permissions to access a specific object, enter the full path of the object. The full path cannot contain the bucket name. For example, to grant users the permissions to access an object named myphoto.png in the abc directory, enter abc/myphoto.png . |
|---|---|
| Authorized User | Select the type of accounts to which you want to grant the permissions. All Accounts (*): Select this option if you want to grant all users the permissions to access the specified resources. Other Accounts: Select this option if you want to grant other Alibaba Cloud accounts, Resource Access Management (RAM) users, or RAM roles the permissions to access the specified resources. |
| Authorized Operation | You can select one of the following options to specify authorized operations: Basic Settings and Advanced Settings. Basic Settings If you select this option, configure the following permissions based on your business requirements. You can move the pointer over the icon to the right of each permission to view the actions that correspond to the permission. Read Only: allows authorized users to view, list, and download the resources. Read/Write: allows authorized users to read and write the resources. Full Access: allows authorized users to perform all operations on the resources. Deny Access: forbids authorized users from performing operations on the resources. Advanced Settings If you select this option, configure the following parameters: Effect: Select Allow or Reject. Actions: Specify the actions that you want to allow or deny. |
| Condition | This parameter is optional. You can configure this parameter in Basic Settings and Advanced Settings to specify the conditions that must be met before users can access OSS resources. Access Method: By default, authorized users can access OSS resources over HTTP and HTTPS. If you want authorized users to access the specified resources in the bucket over HTTPS, select HTTPS. If you want authorized users to access the specified resources in the bucket over HTTP, select HTTP. Compared with HTTP, HTTPS is more secure. If you want to force all requests to access resources in the bucket by using one protocol, such as HTTPS, you must configure the bucket policy by specifying policy statements. IP =: Specify the IP addresses or CIDR blocks that can be used to access OSS resources. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). IP ≠: Specify the IP addresses or CIDR blocks that cannot be used to access OSS resources. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). VPC =: Specify the IDs of the VPCs over which users can access OSS resources. You can select the IDs of the VPCs that belong to the current Alibaba Cloud account from the drop-down list. You can also enter the IDs of the VPCs created by using the current Alibaba Cloud account or another Alibaba Cloud account in the field. VPC ≠: Specify the IDs of the VPCs over which users cannot access OSS resources. You can select the IDs of the VPCs that belong to the current Alibaba Cloud account from the drop-down list. You can also enter the IDs of the VPCs created by using the current Alibaba Cloud account or another Alibaba Cloud account in the field. Note If you specify both the VPC (VPC = or VPC ≠) and IP (IP = or IP ≠) conditions in a bucket policy, the bucket policy must meet both the specified VPC and IP address requirements. |

Object Storage Service (OSS) provides zone-redundant storage (ZRS) and locally redundant storage (LRS) to ensure data durability and availability. LRS provides data redundancy within one zone, and ZRS provides data redundancy across zones.

**Redundancy types**

**ZRS**

For regions with three or more zones, the multi-zone redundancy storage mechanism is implemented. Multiple copies of your data are stored across multiple zones in the same region, which ensures uninterrupted access even if one zone becomes unavailable. For regions with two zones, the dualzone redundancy storage mechanism is implemented. Copies of your data are redundantly stored across the two zones within the same region, which ensures uninterrupted access even if one zone becomes unavailable.

**Important**

ZRS stores multiple data copies across zones in a region. If the region becomes unavailable, your data is inaccessible. If your business application requires higher availability, we recommend that you use cross-region replication to back up your data.

**LRS**

LRS stores multiple copies of your data on multiple devices of different facilities in the same zone. LRS ensures data durability and availability even if hardware failures occur. ZRS is supported only when three-zone disaster recovery is used.

**Create a ZRS bucket**

**Important**

You can also create a ZRS bucket by using the SDK for Java, SDK for Go, or SDK for Python.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click **Create a Bucket**.
3. On the **Create Bucket** page, select a three-zone disaster recovery cluster for **Cluster**, select **Zone-Redundant Storage (ZRS)** for **Redundancy**
**Type**, and configure other parameters.
For more information about the parameters, see Create a bucket.
4. Click **Submit**.
After you submit the request, you can click **OK** in the message that appears to return to the **Overview** tab. After the bucket is created, the
**Redundancy Type** of the bucket is displayed as **ZRS**.

A large number of log entries are generated when Object Storage Service (OSS) resources are accessed. OSS uses Simple Log Service to help you query and collect statistics for OSS access logs and audit access to OSS in the OSS console, track exception events, and troubleshoot problems. This helps you improve work efficiency and make informed decisions.

**Benefits**

Pushes logs to Simple Log Service within three minutes and allows you to view real-time logs in the OSS console. Provides log analysis and common analysis reports for easy data queries. Allows you to query and analyze raw logs in real time and filter logs by bucket name, object name, API operation, or time.

**Prerequisites**

Simple Log Service is activated and is authorized to access OSS.

**Enable real-time log query**

**Important**

If this is your first time enabling real-time log query for a bucket, you must wait for about 1 minute and then refresh the page before you can use this feature. When you enable real-time log query, the system automatically creates a project and a Logstore in Simple Log Service.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **Log Query** tab, click **Activate now**.
After you activate log query, you can view the corresponding project and Logstore in Simple Log Service. The project name is in the `oss-log-<UID>-` `<RegionID>` format. `<UID>` indicates the UID of the organization to which the bucket belongs, and `<RegionID>` indicates the region ID. The Logstore name is oss-log-store.

**Important**

Do not manually delete the automatically generated projects or Logstores. Otherwise, log query exceptions may occur.

**Specify a log retention period**

By default, logs are retained for seven days. You can modify the retention period as needed.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **Log Query** tab, click **Set the log retention time**.
4. In the **Set the log retention time** dialog box, modify the retention period and click **OK**.
Custom data can be retained for 7 to 3,000 days.

**Query real-time logs**

OSS uses Simple Log Service to help you query and collect statistics for OSS access logs and audit access to OSS in the OSS console, track exception events, and troubleshoot problems. This helps you improve work efficiency and make informed decisions. Method 1: Query real-time logs on the **Raw logs** tab i. Log in to the OSS console. ii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage. iii. On the **Log Query** tab, click the **Raw logs** tab and enter a query condition. You can also click the icon to switch to the interactive query and analysis mode. Then, enter query conditions on the **Log Query (Simple**
**Mode)** tab, or select a statistical analysis scenario on the **Statistical Analysis** tab.
A search condition consists of a search statement and an analytic statement and is in the Search statement|Analytic statement format. Example:
* | SELECT status, count(*) AS PV GROUP BY status . The query statement and the analytic statement are separated by a vertical bar (|). The
query statement uses proprietary syntax of Log Service. A query statement can be individually executed. However, an analytic statement must be executed together with a query statement. In other words, analysis is performed based on the query results or the complete data. For more information, see the "Query and analysis" topic of Simple Log Service in the **CDS User Guide**.

| Statement | Description |
|---|---|
| Search statement | A query statement specifies one or more query conditions, and then returns the logs that meet the specified conditions. A query statement can be a keyword, a numeric value, a numeric value range, a space character, or an asterisk (*). If you specify a space character or an asterisk (*) as the query statement, no conditions are specified and all logs are returned. |
| Analytic statement | An analytic statement is used to aggregate or analyze all log data or the log data that meets the specified query conditions in a Logstore. |

iv. Click **15 Minutes(Relative)** to specify a time range for the query statement. You can select a relative time, a time frame, or a custom time range. However, the time range that you can specify is only accurate to the minute at most. If you want to use a time range that is accurate to the second, you must specify the time range in the analytic statement. Example: * |

```
SELECT * FROM log WHERE __time__>1558013658 AND __time__< 1558013660 .
```

v. Click **Search & Analyze**. Query results contain query and analysis results in a log distribution histogram, on the Raw Logs tab, and on the Graph tab. You can also perform operations on the results. For example, you can configure alerts and create saved searches. For more information, see the "Query and analyze logs" topic in the **Simple Log Service User Guide**. Log distribution histogram The log distribution histogram shows the distribution of returned logs in different periods of time. Raw logs You can click the Table or Raw Data option on the **Raw Logs** tab to analyze the distribution of a field over a period of time, view the context of the specified log in the raw file, monitor the log content in real time, and extract key log information. On the **Graph** tab, you can view the visual query and analysis results, add charts to the dashboard, download logs, and configure interactive behaviors. On the **LogReduce** tab, you can click **Enable LogReduce** to aggregate similar logs during log collection. Method 2: Query real-time logs on the **Log Reports** tab i. Log in to the OSS console. ii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage. iii. Click the **Log Query** tab. Then, click the **Log Report** tab in the upper-left corner to view log analysis reports. The Log Reports tab provides four types of ready-to-use reports.
**Access Center**: displays the overall operating status including the PV, UV, traffic, and distribution of access over the Internet.
**Audit Center**: displays statistics of object operations including read, write, and delete operations.
**Operation Center**: displays statistics of access logs including the number of requests and distribution of failed operations.
**Performance Center**: displays statistics of performance including the performance of downloads and uploads over the Internet, the
performance of transmission over different networks or with different object sizes, and the list of differences between stored and downloaded objects.

**Disable real-time log query**

**Important**

If you disable real-time log query, the system does not delete the automatically generated Simple Log Service projects and Logstores. Delete the projects before you disable real-time log query.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **Log Query** page, click **Close associated logs** in the upper-right corner.
You can encapsulate multiple image processing (IMG) parameters in a style and perform complex IMG operations by using the style.

**Background information**

Up to 50 styles can be created for a bucket. These styles can be used only for image objects in the bucket.

**Create a style**

1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. Click the **Image processing** tab. On this tab, click **Create a new style**.
4. On the **Basic Edit** or **Advanced editing** tab of the **Create a new style** panel, specify a rule name, an image path, and a style.
You can create an image style by in **Basic Editing** or **Advanced Editing** mode.
**Basic Editing**: provides a graphical user interface (GUI) that allows you to choose the IMG methods, such as resizing an image, adding a
watermark, and modifying the image format.
**Advanced Editing**: You can create an image style rule by adding code to the code field. Enter the code in the

| image/action1,parame_value1/action2,parame_value2/... |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| For example, | image/resize,p_63/quality,q_90 | is used to |

For example, `image/resize,p_63/quality,q_90` is used to resize an image to 63% of its original size and change the relative quality of the image to 90%. If you want to add image and text watermarks to images at the same time by using a style, use **Advanced Editing** to create the style.
5. Click **OK**.

**Apply a style**

After a style is created, you can use the style to process your image objects in the bucket.
1. On the Buckets page, click the **File management** tab.
2. Click the name of the image that you want to apply a style to.
3. In the **Details** panel, select an image style from the **Image Style** drop-down list.
You can view the processed image in the **Details** panel. Right-click the image and click **Save As** to save the image to your local disk.

**Simplify IMG URLs that include style parameters**

An IMG URL that has a style contains a file access URL, style parameters, and a style name. Example: `https://image-demo.oss-cn-qd-ase-d01-a.mytest-` inc.com/example.jpg?x-oss-process=style/small . You can replace the ?x-oss-process=style/ field with a custom delimiter to simplify the IMG URL. For example, if you specify the delimiter as an exclamation point (!), the IMG URL can be simplified to `https://image-demo.oss-cn-qd-ase-d01-a.mytest-`

```
inc.com/example.jpg!small .
```

1. On the Buckets page, click the **Image processing** tab.
2. Click **Access settings**.
3. In the **Access settings** panel, select a delimiter below the **Custom delimiter** parameter.
Only hyphens (-), underscores (_), forward slashes (/), and exclamation points (?) can be used as delimiters.
4. Click **OK**.

**Manage styles**

After a style is created, you can export, edit, or delete the style based on your business requirements.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| Export a style | Click Export Style to export all style configurations of the bucket to a local file. |
| Modify a style | You can modify the IMG method for a style, such as Format Conversion, Resize Type, and Brightness. 1. Find the style that you want to modify and clickE dit in the Actions column. 2. In the Edit dialog box, modify the IMG method for the style based on your business requirements. 3. Click OK. |
| Delete a style | Use one of the following methods to delete one or more styles. Important Deleted styles cannot be recovered. Proceed with caution. To delete a single style, find the style that you want to delete and clickD elete in the Actions column. In the message that appears, click OK. To delete multiple styles at a time, select the styles that you want to delete and clickD elete below the style list. In the message that appears, click OK. |

OSS provides the source image protection feature to protect your images from being used by unauthorized anonymous requesters. After you enable source image protection for your bucket, anonymous requesters can access images in the bucket only by adding style parameters in the requests or by using signed URLs.

**Background information**

You can use the following methods to access the images: Use the file URL that contains the style parameters in the format of https://BucketName.Endpoint/ObjectName?x-oss-process=style/StyleName . Use the file URL that contains a signature in the format of https://BucketName.Endpoint/ObjectName?Signature .
1. Log on to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. Click the **Image Processing (IMG)** tab. On the page that appears, click **Access Settings**.
4. In the **Access Settings** panel, turn on **Protect Source Image File** and configure the parameters described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Protected File Extensions | Select a file suffix from the Protected File Extensions drop-down list. All objects in the bucket that match the specified suffix are protected. |
| Delimiters | If you set the custom delimiter, use the delimiter to replace ? x-oss-process=style/ to further simplify the IMG URL. OSS supports the following delimiters: hyphens (-), underscores (), forward slashes (/), and exclamation points (!). _ Click the check box before the delimiter that you want to select. For example, if you set the delimiter to an exclamation point (!), the IMG URL can be simplified to http(s)//:BucketName.Endpoint/ObjectName!StyleName . |

5. Click **Confirm**.
Q: Why is HTTP status code 403 returned when I directly access a protected image, whereas HTTP status code 200 is returned when I access the image over Content Delivery Network (CDN)? A: One possible cause is that the request is redirected to access a private bucket over CDN. Source image protection is applicable only to objects that are accessed by anonymous users. Q: How can my source image still be accessed by using a signed URL when source image protection is enabled for the image? Source image protection applies only to objects that can be accessed by anonymous users. Access by signed URLs is not anonymous. Therefore, the source image can be accessed by using a signed URL even if you enable source image protection. In cluster-disaster recovery scenarios, if you want to synchronize objects encrypted by using CMKs managed by KMS to the destination bucket, you must use a role that has permissions to manage and decrypt the objects by using CMKs. In this case, you can use the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole or create a custom role.

**Bind a predefined role**

You can create a service-linked role that is attached to the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole to authorize OSS to view and perform operations on other resources in the organization.
1. Go to the **Service-linked Roles** page.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.d ii. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Service-linked Roles**.
2. On the **Service-linked Roles** page, click **Create Service-linked Role**.
3. On the page that appears, select Object Storage Service from the **Service Name** drop-down list and select an organization from the **Authorized**
**Organization Name** drop-down list.
The organization of the service-linked role must be the same as that of the bucket in which the objects need to be encrypted by using CMKs are stored.
4. Click **OK**.
On the **Service-linked Roles** page, you can click Details in the Actions column corresponding to the predefined role AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole to view the information about the role. Click the **Role Details** tab to view the following information: Role Name: AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRole Trust Policy: `{`

```json
  "Statement": [
```

      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": [
          "oss.aliyuncs.com"
```

`]` `}` `}` `],`

  "Version": "1"
```

`}` Click the **Role Policy** tab and view the following information: Policy Name: AliyunOSSPrivateCloudDrsSyncRolePolicy Description: `{`

        "Effect": "Allow",

             "kms:Encrypt",
