```json
        "Effect": "Allow"
```

`}]` `}`

**Create a custom role**

You can create custom roles to control the permissions of users at different granularity levels. To synchronize objects encrypted by using CMKs managed by KMS to the destination bucket, the custom role that you create must have permissions to manage, encrypt, and decrypt the objects by using CMKs. You can perform the following steps to create the custom role:
1. Go to the **Role authorization** page.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. iii. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions > Role Permissions**.
2. In the upper-left corner of the **Role authorization** page, click **Create Custom Role**.
3. In the Basic configuration step of the **Create Custom Role** wizard, click **Advanced Settings**, and then click **Create RAM Role & Attach Policy** .
4. On the **Create RAM Role & Attach Policy** page, set the parameters described in the following table and then click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Role name | The name of the role that you want to create. The name can be up to 64 characters in length and can contain only letters and digits. |
| Description | Optional. The description of the role. The description can be up to 500 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, commas (,), semicolons (;), and underscores (). _ |
| Sharing Scope | The scope in which the role is visible. Valid values: Global: This role is visible and valid for all organizations. |

5. Create a policy.
i. In the upper-right corner of the policy list, click **Create Policy**. ii. In the **Create Policy** dialog box, configure the parameters described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Policy Name | The name of the policy you want to create. The name must be 2 to 50 characters in length and can contain only letters and digits. The name must be unique in the system. |
| Sharing Scope | The scope in which the policy is visible. Valid value: Global. This value indicates that the role is visible and valid for all organizations. |
| Description | The description of the policy. |
| Policy Content | The permissions defined by this policy. The policy content is in JSON format. The following code provides an example of policy content: { "Version": "1", "Statement": [ { "Action": "oss:*", "Effect": "Allow", "Resource": "*" }, { "Action": "oss:PutBucket*", "Effect": "Deny", "Resource": "*" }, { "Action": [ "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey", "kms:GenerateDataKey"], "Resource": "*", "Effect": "Allow" }] } |

iii. Click **OK**. Click **Next**.
6. Modify the trust policy and then click **Next**.
i. Click **Modify Trust Policy**. ii. The trust policy is in JSON format. The following code provides an example of a trust policy: `{`

```json
  "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": [
          "oss.aliyuncs.com"
```

`]` `}` `}` `],`

```json
  "Version": "1"
```

`}` iii. Click **Save Changes**.
7. Confirm the information about the custom role. Click **Create**.
After the custom role is created, you can view the information about the role on the **Role authorization** page. If you no longer use the role that you create, choose
> **Delete** in the **Actions** column corresponding to the role in the **Role authorization**
page to delete the role.
8. Create a RAM role for the custom role.
i. On the **Role authorization** page, click the name of the custom role that you create. ii. On the details page of the custom role, click the **RAM Role** tab and then click **Create**. iii. In the **Create** dialog box, select an organization. In scenarios where you use the custom role to synchronize objects encrypted by using CMKs in a bucket, the organization of the RAM role must be the same as that of the bucket. iv. Click **OK**. After the RAM user is created, you can view the information about the RAM user on the **RAM Role** tab. If you no longer use the RAM role that you create, click **Remove** in the **Actions** column corresponding to the RAM role on the **RAM Role** page to delete the RAM role.

### 2.6 Objects

You can search for objects whose names contain specific prefixes in buckets or folders in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.

**Prerequisites**

An object is uploaded to the bucket. For more information, see Upload an object.

**Background information**

When you search for objects based on a prefix, search strings are case-sensitive and cannot contain forward slashes (/). You can search for objects only in the root directory of the current bucket or in the current directory. Directories and objects stored in subdirectories cannot be searched.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, search for objects.
Search for objects and subdirectories in the root directory. Enter the specified object name prefix in the search box. Objects and subdirectories whose names contain the specified prefix within the root directory of the bucket are displayed. Search for objects and subdirectories in a specified directory Click the directory, and then enter the specified object name prefix in the search box. Objects and subdirectories whose names contain the specified prefix within the current directory are displayed. This topic describes how to configure the access control list (ACL) of an object to control access to the object.

**Prerequisites**

An object is uploaded to the bucket. For more information, see Upload an object.
1. Log in to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, find the object that you want to manage and choose **... > Set read and write permissions** in the **Operation**
column. Alternatively, click the name of the object whose ACL you want to configure. In the **Details** panel, click **Set read and write permissions** in the
**File ACL** section.
4. In the **Set read and write permissions** panel, configure the ACL of the object.
You can set the ACL of the object to one of the following values:
**Inherited Bucket**: The ACL of the object is the same as that of the bucket.
**Private**: Only the object owner can perform read and write operations on the object. Other users cannot access the object.
**Public Reading**: Only the object owner can write data to the object. Other users, including anonymous users, can only read the object.
**Public Read/Write**: All users, including anonymous users, can perform read and write operations on the object. Exercise caution when you set the
ACL to this value.
5. Click **Submit**.
Object metadata includes standard HTTP headers and user metadata. Configure HTTP headers to control caching, content type, and download behavior. Add user metadata to tag objects with custom key-value pairs.

**Background information**

You can configure object metadata for up to 100 objects at a time in the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, use one of the following methods to open the **Set HTTP header** panel:
Configure HTTP headers for multiple objects Select one or more objects and click **Set HTTP header** below the object list. Configure HTTP headers for a single object Method 1: Find the object that you want to manage and click **Set HTTP header** in the **Operation** column. Method 2: Click the name of the object that you want to manage. In the **Details** panel, find the object that you want to manage and click **Set HTTP**
**header** in the **Type** section.
4. In the **Set HTTP header** panel, set the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |   |
|---|---|---|
| Content-Type | Select the object type. The browser determines the default method that is used to open an object based on the selected object type. For example, the value of the Content-Type parameter for a GIF image is image/gif . |   |
| Content-Encoding | Enter the encoding method of the object. You must specify this header based on the encoding type of the object. Otherwise, the browser that serves as the client may fail to parse the encoding type of the object, or the object may fail to be downloaded. If the object is not encoded, leave this header empty. Valid values: identity (default): OSS does not compress or encode the object. gzip: OSS uses the LZ77 compression algorithm created by Lempel and Ziv in 1977 and 32-bit cyclic redundancy check (CRC) to encode the object. compress: OSS uses the Lempel–Ziv–Welch (LZW) compression algorithm to encode the object. deflate: OSS uses the zlib library and the deflate algorithm to encode the object. br: OSS uses the Brotli algorithm to encode the object. For more information about Content-Encoding, see RFC 2616. Important If you want static web page objects, such as HTML, JavaScript, XML, and JSON objects, to be compressed into GZIP objects when you access the objects, you must leave this header empty and add the Accept- Encoding: gzip header to your request. |   |
| Content-Language | Enter the language of the object content. For example, if the content of an object is written in simplified Chinese, you can set this parameter to zh-CN . |   |
| Content-Disposition | Enter the method used to access the object. Valid values: inline: The object is directly opened in the browser. To ensure that an image object or a web page object is previewed but not downloaded when the object is accessed, you must set Content-Disposition to inline and use the custom domain name mapped to the bucket to access the object. attachment: The object is downloaded to the local computer. For example, if this header is set to attachment; filename="example.jpg" and the object is downloaded to the on-premises computer, the object is named example.jpg on the on-premises computer. For more information about Content-Disposition, see RFC 2616. |   |
| Cache-Control | Enter cache configurations for the object. Valid values: no-cache: The object can be cached on the client or on the browser of the proxy server. However, each time you access the object, OSS checks whether the cached object is available. If the cache is available, you can directly access the cache. Otherwise, the access request is sent to OSS. no-store: All content of the object is not cached. public: All content of the object is cached. private: All content of the object is cached only on the client. For more information about Cache-Control, see RFC 2616. |   |
| Expires | Enter the expiration time of the cache in UTC. Example: 2022-10-12T00:00:00.000Z . If max-age= <seconds> is included in the Cache-Control header settings, max-age=<seconds> takes precedence over the value of Expires. |   |
| User-defined metadata | Add the user metadata of the object. To add multiple user metadata headers for an object, clickA dd entry and set the parameters. However, the total size of user metadata of the object cannot exceed 8 KB. When you add user metadata, user metadata headers must be prefixed with x-oss-meta- and assigned values. Example: x-oss-meta-last-modified:20200909u . |   |

| Accept- |   |   |
|---|---|---|

|   |   | Encoding: gzip |
|---|---|---|

| max-age= |   |
|---|---|

|   | <seconds> |
|---|---|

5. Click **OK**.
Symbolic links are a convenient way to access frequently used objects in a bucket. After creation, you can use a symbolic link like a Windows shortcut to access the target object.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
You can enter the name of the bucket in the Bucket Name search box to quickly find the bucket.
3. On the page that appears, click the **Object Management** tab.
4. Find the object that you want to manage and choose **More** > **Configure Symbolic Link** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Configure Symbolic Link** panel, enter the name of the symbolic link in the **Symbolic Link File or Folder** field and click **OK**.
The name of a symbolic link must comply with the following conventions: Example: filename or aaa/bbb/filename. The name cannot contain emojis. You can use forward slashes (/) to specify subdirectories. However, the name cannot start with a forward slash (/) or a backslash (\), or contain consecutive forward slashes (/). The name cannot contain subdirectories that are named two consecutive periods (..). The name must be 1 to 254 characters in length.

**Important**

If the name of a symbolic link does not include the object name extension, such as the symbolic link named myphoto for the myphoto.jpg object, you can preview the object when you access the symbolic link in the OSS console or by using its URL. When you use a tool or the OSS console to download the object by using the symbolic link, the format of the downloaded object is unknown, and the object cannot be directly opened. To open the object, you must add the correct object name extension when you create a symbolic link for the object. You can execute SQL statements to extract and download content from individual CSV or JSON objects.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Buckets page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
You can enter the name of the bucket in the Bucket Name search box to quickly find the bucket.
3. Click the **Object Management** tab, find the object that you want to manage and choose **More > Select Content** in the **Actions** column.
4. In the **Select Content** panel, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| File type | The type of the file. CSV or JSON files are supported. |
| Separator | This parameter is required only if you set the File type parameter to CSV. You can select a comma (,) or enter a custom separator. |
| The file has a header line. | This parameter is required only if you set the File type parameter to CSV. If the first row of the file contains column headers, the header row is excluded from the extracted data after this switch is turned on. |
| JSON format character | This parameter is required only if you set the File type parameter to JSON. JSONLINES _ JSONDOCUMENT _ |
| File Size | The size of the current file. |
| Compressed format | The compression format of the file. Valid values: NONE GZIP |

5. Click **Show file preview** to preview the content of the file.
6. Click **Next Step**. In the SQL editor, enter and execute an SQL statement to extract the required file content.
7. Click **Execute**. In the **Execution result** section, view the extracted file content.
Click **Download** in the lower part of the **Execution result** section to download the extracted file content to your on-premises machine. You can use the Object Storage Service (OSS) console to create and simulate basic features of directories in Windows. This topic describes how to create a directory in the OSS console.

**Background information**

OSS does not use a hierarchical structure to store objects. Instead, it uses a flat structure. All elements are stored in buckets as objects. To help you organize objects and simplify management, the OSS console displays objects whose names end with a forward slash (/) as directories. The objects can be uploaded and downloaded. You can use directories in the OSS console in the same manner as you use directories in Windows. The OSS console displays objects whose names end with a forward slash (/) as directories, regardless of whether these objects contain data. The objects can only be downloaded by calling an API operation or by using OSS SDKs.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, click **Create a directory**.
4. In the **Create a directory** panel, enter a name for the directory.
The directory name must comply with the following conventions: The name can contain only UTF-8 characters and cannot contain emojis. The name cannot start with a forward slash (/) or backslash (\). The name cannot contain consecutive forward slashes (/). You can use forward slashes (/) in a directory name to quickly create a subdirectory. For example, when you create a directory named example/test/, the directory named example/ is created in the root directory of the bucket and the subdirectory named test/ is created in the example/ directory. The name cannot be two consecutive periods ( `..` ). The directory name must be 1 to 254 characters in length.
5. Click **OK**.
After you create a directory, you can click **Delete completely** in the Operation column to delete the directory and the data in the directory. After you upload objects to a bucket, you can download the objects to the default download path of your browser or a specific on-premises path.
1. Log in to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. Click the **File management** tab, and then download single or multiple objects.
Download a single object Method 1: Find the object that you want to download and choose **... > Download** in the **Operation** column. Method 2: Click the name of the object that you want to download. In the **Details** panel, find the object and click **Download** below the **URL** parameter. Download multiple objects at a time Select the objects that you want to download and click **Download** below the object list. You can download up to 100 objects at a time in the OSS console. You can delete uploaded objects if they are no longer needed.

**Background information**

You can delete a single object or multiple objects at the same time. You can delete up to 100 objects at a time. To delete specific objects or delete more than 100 objects at the same time, we recommend that you use API operations or OSS SDKs.

**Important**

Deleted objects cannot be recovered. Proceed with caution.
1. Log in to the Object Storage Service (OSS) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, delete one or more objects.
Delete a single object Find the object that you want to delete and choose in the **Operation** column. Delete multiple objects at the same time Select the objects that you want to delete and click **Delete** below the object list.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
When you use multipart upload to upload an object, the object is split into several parts. After all parts are uploaded to the Object Storage Service (OSS) server, you can call the CompleteMultipartUpload API operation to combine them into a complete object.

**Background information**

You can also configure lifecycle rules to clear parts that are not needed on a regular basis. For more information, see Configure a lifecycle rule.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Buckets. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** page, click **Fragmentation management**.
4. In the **Debris Management (Multipart)** panel, delete the parts.
To delete all parts in the bucket, select all parts and click **Delete all**. To delete specific parts in the bucket, select these parts and click **Delete**.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
Object Storage Service (OSS) supports object tagging. You can add tags to objects to classify the objects. A tag is a key-value pair that can be used to identify objects. You can perform operations on multiple objects that have the same tag. For example, you can configure lifecycle rules for objects that have the same tag.

**Background information**

A tag is a key-value pair that can be used to identify objects. You can manage multiple objects that have the same tag. For example, you can configure lifecycle rules for objects that have the same tag or authorize Resource Access Management (RAM) users to access objects that have the same tag. When you add tags to objects, take note of the following items: A maximum of 10 tags can be configured for each object. The tags of the same object must have unique tag keys. A tag key can be up to 128 bytes in length. A tag value can be up to 256 bytes in length. Tag keys and tag values are case-sensitive. The key and value of a tag can contain letters, digits, spaces, and the following characters: + - = _ : / Only the bucket owner and authorized users have read and write permissions on object tags. These permissions are independent of object access control lists (ACLs). In cross-region replication (CRR), object tags are also replicated to the destination bucket.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket that you want to manage.
3. On the **File management** tab, find the object that you want to manage and click **Label** in the **Operation** column.
4. In the **Label** panel, click **Add entry** and set the **Key** and **Value** parameters.
You can click **Add entry** to add up to 10 tags to the object. To delete a tag, click the icon to the right of the tag.
5. Click **Submit**.

**2.6.11. Configure bucket policies to authorize other users to access OSS**

**resources**

You can configure bucket policies to authorize other users to access specific resources in an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket.

**Background information**

You can configure multiple bucket policies for a bucket. The total size of the policies cannot exceed 16 KB.

**Method 1: Configure bucket policies by using the GUI**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Buckets**. On the Bucket List page, click the name of the bucket for which you want to configure bucket policies.
3. On the **File management** tab, click **Authorization**.
4. On the **Graphic settings** tab, click **Add authorization**.
5. In the **Add authorization** dialog box, configure the parameters and click **OK**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Authorized resources | Select the resources on which you want to grant other users the access permissions. Valid values: Entire Bucket: The bucket policy applies to all resources in the bucket. Specific Resources: The bucket policy applies only to specific resources in the bucket. You can configure multiple bucket policies for specific resources in a bucket. Directory-level authorization To configure a bucket policy to grant users the permissions to access all subdirectories and objects in a directory, add an asterisk (*) after the name of the directory. For example, to grant users the permissions to access all subdirectories and objects in a directory named abc, enter abc/* . Object-level authorization To configure a bucket policy to grant users the permissions to access a specific object, enter the full path of the object. The full path cannot contain the bucket name. For example, to grant users the permissions to access an object named myphoto.png in the abc directory, enter abc/myphoto.png . |
| Resource Paths | Specify the paths of authorized resources. |
| Authorized User | Select the type of accounts to which you want to grant the permissions. All Accounts (*): Select this option if you want to grant all users, including anonymous users, the permissions to access the specified resources. Other Accounts: Select this option if you want to grant other Alibaba Cloud accounts, Resource Access Management (RAM) users, or temporary users generated based on Security Token Service (STS) the permissions to access the specified resources. To grant other Alibaba Cloud accounts or RAM users the permissions to access the specified resources, enter the UIDs of the Alibaba Cloud accounts or RAM users. To grant temporary users generated based on STS the permissions to access the specified resources, specify the users in the following format: arn:sts::{RoleOwnerUid}:assumed-role/{RoleName}/{RoleSessionName} . Assume that the role used to grant permissions to a temporary user is testrole, the UID of the Apsara Stack tenant account that owns the role is 12345, and the RoleSessionName that is specified when the temporary user is generated is testsession. In this case, enter arn:sts::12345:assumed-role/testrole/testsession . To grant all temporary users the permissions to access the specified resources, use asterisks (*) as wildcard characters. For example, enter arn:sts::*:*/*/* . Important If an authorized user is a user that uses a temporary token generated by STS, the user cannot access the specified resources in the OSS console. |

| Authorized Operation | You can select one of the following options to specify authorized operations: Simple Settings and Advanced Settings. Simple Settings If you select this option, configure the following permissions based on your business requirements. You can move the pointer over the icon to the right of each permission to view the actions that correspond to the permission. Read-only: allows authorized users to view, list, and download the resources. Read/Write: allows authorized users to perform read and write operations on the resources. Complete Control: allows authorized users to perform all operations on the resources. Access Denied: forbids authorized users from performing operations on the resources. Important If multiple bucket policies are configured for a user, the user has all the permissions defined in the policies. However, the policy in which Authorized Operation is set to Access Denied takes precedence. For example, if you configure a policy to grant the Read-only permission to a user, and then configure another policy to grant the Read/Write permission to the same user, the permission of the user is Read/Write. If you configure a third policy to grant the Access Denied permission to the user, the permission of the user is Access Denied. Advanced Settings If you select this option, configure the following parameters: Effectiveness: Select Allow or Reject. Operation: Specify the actions that you want to allow or deny. |
|---|---|
| Condition | This parameter is optional. You can configure this parameter in Basic Settings and Advanced Settings to specify the conditions that must be met before users can access OSS resources. Access Method: Select HTTPS or HTTP. IP =: Specify the IP addresses or CIDR blocks that can be used to access OSS resources. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). IP ≠: Specify the IP addresses or CIDR blocks that cannot be used to access OSS resources. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). VPC =: Specify the VPC ID that belongs to a VPC account. VPC ≠: Specify the VPC ID that does not belong to a VPC account. |

6. Click **OK**.

### 2.10 CSG

Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) is a gateway service that can be deployed on Apsara Stack. CSG uses OSS buckets as backend storage devices. CSG provides on-premises and cloud applications with standard file services over the Network File System (NFS) and Server Message Block (SMB) protocols. CSG supports only file gateways. File gateways use OSS buckets as backend storage devices, and map the object directory structure of OSS buckets to NAS file systems. You can read and write all objects in a specified OSS bucket over standard NFS and SMB protocols. CSG also uses on-premises storage to cache hot data, and provides high-performance data access in addition to the large storage capacity of OSS buckets. File gateways are compatible with the Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX) and third-party backup software.

**Service architecture**

The following figure shows the architecture of CSG.

**Scenarios**

Build a file storage service for a large file system when local storage is limited. Store data as objects in the cloud, and allow applications to access the data in a file system without the need to modify code. Before you use Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG), we recommend that you read the following usage notes. You can create file gateways only by using the recommended CIDR block or its subnets of a virtual private cloud (VPC). You may have a large number of files stored in the same directory of an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket. For example, hundreds of thousands or even millions of subdirectories or files exist in the root directory or under a specific directory of an OSS bucket. In this case, file gateways are not suitable due to extremely slow access to these subdirectories or files. In most cases, if you want to use file gateways to manage files, we recommend that you place at most 100,000 files in a single directory. Files gateways reserve 20% of the cache disk space to cache metadata and use the remaining space to cache data. The stored metadata refers to the metadata of different files, including the size and last modification time of each file. In this case, if a file is discarded, a file gateway creates a metadata file so that you can view the information about the discarded file when you access folders from the client. If you want to read the discarded file, the file gateway retrieves the data of the discarded file from the OSS bucket to the cache disk. The space required to cache the metadata on the cache disk determines the maximum number of files that are supported by the current share. In most cases, a share with a cache disk of 100 GiB in size supports at most 10 million files. You can check the value of the Available Metadata Space parameter of shares when you use the file gateway. Typically, you may need to expand the cache space when the remaining space is about 3 GiB. Files written to file gateways are asynchronously synchronized to OSS buckets. Before the files are synchronized to OSS buckets by using file gateways, we recommend that you do not modify or delete the files by using other gateways or tools, such as ossutil or ossfs. Otherwise, data inconsistency may occur. We recommend that you do not frequently interrupt the upload of large files to NFS or SMB shares. The system uploads files by using multipart uploads. If you interrupt the upload of large files, file fragments are generated in the corresponding OSS bucket. These file fragments occupy the storage space of the OSS bucket. Therefore, the storage usage of the OSS bucket is slightly higher than the total file size. The cache capacity for file sharing is calculated based on the following formula: Recommended local cache capacity = [Application bandwidth (Mbit/s) - Backend bandwidth of a gateway (Mbit/s)] × Write duration (seconds) × 1.2. To obtain better performance when you access data from local clients, you can estimate the total amount of hot data, compare the total amount of hot data with the recommended on-premises cache capacity, and select the higher value as the capacity of the on-premises cache disk. If you want to write large files by using a file gateway, the size of each file must be smaller than 30% of the cache disk capacity. You cannot write multiple large files at the same time. If you write multiple large files at the same time, the cache disk space is exhausted. File gateways support sparse files. If a sparse file fails to be uploaded to a file gateway, run the following command to convert the format of the sparse file:

```
dd if=<sparse file name> of=<sparse file name> conv=notrunc bs=1M
```

The size of the sparse file cannot exceed the remaining capacity of the cache disk. The names of files and directories on a file gateway must be encoded in UTF-8. File gateways do not support file or directory names that are encoded in a format other than UTF-8. For example, if you mount an NFS share of a file gateway on a Windows client, the files and directories whose names contain Chinese characters cannot be created. In this case, a 0x8007045D error is reported. If the size of a file on a file gateway exceeds 256 MiB, we recommend that you disable versioning for the associated OSS bucket. Otherwise, a timeout error may occur when the gateway uploads metadata. This compromises the performance of the gateway. This topic describes the limits of Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG). CSG is an independently deployed cloud service. A CSG instance cannot be mapped to an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket that is associated with a virtual private cloud (VPC) or with a single tunnel. A CSG instance cannot be mapped to an OSS bucket for which the write once read many (WORM) feature is enabled. CSG cannot detect the capacity threshold that is configured for an OSS bucket. When the data in an OSS bucket to which a CSG instance is mapped exceeds the capacity threshold, subsequent data that is written into the CSG instance cannot be synchronized to the bucket. A CSG instance cannot be mapped to an OSS bucket that is deployed in a different region. Make sure that your CSG instance and OSS bucket are deployed in the same region. After you use file gateways to map the objects and directories in Object Storage Service (OSS) buckets to the files and directories in Apsara File Storage NAS (NAS) file systems, you can read and write all objects in a specific OSS bucket by using the Network File System (NFS) and Server Message Block (SMB) protocols. Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) uses on-premises storage to cache hot data, and provides high-performance data access in addition to the large storage capacity of OSS buckets.

**Prerequisites**

A virtual private cloud (VPC) and a vSwitch are created. For more information, see the "Create a VPC" and "Create a vSwitch" topics in **Apsara Stack**
**VPC User Guide**.
An OSS bucket is created. For more information, see Create a bucket. An Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance is created and used as a client, and the ECS instance is associated with the created VPC. For more information, see the "Create an instance" topic in **Apsara Stack ECS User Guide**.

**Background information**

CSG is a gateway service that can be deployed at your self-managed data center or on Apsara Stack. CSG uses OSS buckets as backend storage devices. CSG provides on-premises and cloud applications with standard file services over the NFS and SMB protocols by using cost-efficient virtual machines.

**Step 1: Create a gateway**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
3. If this is your first time using CSG, you must authorize CSG to access other Apsara Stack services based on your business requirements.
When you authorize CSG to access other Apsara Stack services, the service-linked role AliyunServiceRoleForHCSSGW is automatically created. The system attaches the AliyunServiceRolePolicyForHCSSGW policy to this service-linked role. In this case, CSG can assume the service-linked role and access other Apsara Stack services, such as OSS, VPC, and ECS. CSG provides a mount protocol based on the granted permissions to manage requests to OSS buckets, such as the requests to upload, download, or access data in OSS buckets. i. In the **Storage Gateway service authorization** message, read the authorization information and click **Authorize Now**. ii. Complete the authorization as prompted.
4. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, click **Create**.
5. In the **Create a gateway** dialog box, set the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Gateway name | Enter a name for the gateway instance. |
| Description | Enter a description for the gateway. |
| VPC | Select the VPC in which you want to deploy the gateway. Important You must select the VPC in which the ECS instance resides. |
| Virtual Switch | Select the vSwitch that you want to connect to the gateway. Important You must select the vSwitch to which the ECS instance is connected. |
| Gateway ECS specifications | After you select a vSwitch, you can view the specifications of the ECS instance, the number of vCPU cores, memory size, and internal bandwidth. |

6. Click **OK**.
After the gateway is created, the system automatically deploys and starts the gateway. It takes about 5 to 10 minutes to complete the process. The gateway enters the **Running** state if it is activated and deployed.

**Step 2: (Optional) Create an SMB user**

If you want to access SMB shares as an SMB user, you must create an SMB user in advance. By default, if you have not created an SMB user, you can access SMB shares as a public user. However, if you have created an SMB user, you must grant read and write or read-only permissions to the user before you access SMB shares as the SMB user. For more information, see the "Configure an SMB share" section of the Manage shares topic.
1. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, find the gateway for which you want to create an SMB user and click the ID of the gateway.
2. On the page that appears, click the **SMB users** tab.
3. On the **SMB users** page, click **Create User** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the **Add SMB User** dialog box, enter the username and password of the SMB user.
5. Click **OK**.

**Step 3: Create a share**

1. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, find the gateway for which you want to create a share and click the ID of the gateway.
2. On the **Share List** tab, click **Create**.
3. In the **Create a share** dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Custom Bucket domain name | Specify whether to use a custom domain name for the OSS bucket. Valid values: Yes: uses a custom domain name for the OSS bucket. If you select Yes, you can access a bucket that resides in a region different from that in which the specified gateway resides. No (default): uses the default domain name of the OSS bucket in the current region. If you select No, you can access only a bucket that resides in the same region as the specified gateway. |
| Bucket domain name | Select the endpoint of the bucket. |
| Bucket name | Enter the name of the bucket. |
| Subdirectory | If you select Subdirectory, enter the names of the subdirectories of the OSS bucket in the field. |
| Connect to a Bucket using SSL | Specify whether to connect to the OSS bucket by using SSL. Valid values: Yes (default): uses SSL to connect to the OSS bucket. This is the default value. No: does not use SSL to connect to the OSS bucket. |
| BucketAK | The AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret that are used to access the OSS bucket when you specify a custom domain name for the OSS bucket. This parameter is required only if you use a custom domain name of the OSS bucket. Important The account to which the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret belong must have the required permissions to access the OSS bucket. For more information about the permissions on OSS buckets, see Permissions required by a gateway to operate OSS buckets. |
| BucketSK |   |
| Share Name | Enter a name for the NFS or SMB share. If you set the Agreement parameter to NFS, the share name also specifies the virtual path of NFS version 4 (NFSv4). The name can be up to 32 characters in length and can contain letters and digits. The name must start with a letter. |
| Agreement | Select the type of protocol used by the share. Valid values: NFS: The NFS protocol is suitable if you need to access OSS buckets from a Linux operating system. SMB: The SMB protocol is suitable if you need to access OSS buckets from a Windows operating system. |
| Create cache | Create a cache disk. Turn on Create cache and set the Cache type and Cache size parameters. Cache type: Select Effective cloud disk, SSD, Common performance cloud disk, or High- Performance Cloud Disk based on your business requirements. Cache size: Specify a value between 100 and 4096. Unit: GiB. |
| Cache | Select an existing cache disk. If no cache disk is available, turn onC reate cache and then set the Cache type and Cache size parameters. Note 20% of the cache disk space is used to cache metadata. |

| User Mapping | Select the user mapping between the NFS client and the NFS server. This parameter is available only when you set the Agreement parameter to NFS. Valid values: none: NFS client users are not mapped to the nobody user on the NFS server. rootsquash: restricts the root user permissions. NFS clients that use the root identity are mapped to the _ nobody user on the NFS server. allsquash: restricts all user permissions. The NFS client is mapped to the nobody user on the NFS server _ regardless of the identity that the client uses. allanonymous: restricts all user permissions. The NFS client is mapped to the anonymous user on the _ NFS server regardless of the identity that the client uses. |
|---|---|
| Browsable | Specify whether the SMB share can be discovered by network neighbors. This parameter is available only when you set the Agreement parameter to SMB. Valid values: Yes: The SMB share can be discovered by network neighbors. No: The SMB share cannot be discovered by network neighbors. |
| Advanced Settings | To configure advanced settings such as reverse synchronization, turn onA dvanced Settings. Note If an object exists in the current OSS bucket, the reverse synchronization feature is automatically enabled. If you want to disable this feature, you can set Reverse synchronization to No in the Advanced Settings section. After you disable the reverse synchronization feature, objects that exist in the OSS bucket before you mount the share cannot be discovered by the gateway. Mode: Select the mode in which data is saved. Valid values: Copy mode: In this mode, two backups are created for all data. One backup is stored on the on- premises cache disk, and the other backup is stored in the associated OSS bucket. In this mode, the total size of files that can be written to the gateway is equal to the specified size of the cache disk. Cache mode: In this mode, the backup that is stored on the on-premises cache disk contains only metadata and frequently accessed user data. Full data is stored in OSS. In this mode, the total size of files that can be written to the gateway is not affected by the size of the cache disk. We recommend that you select the cache mode if you want to migrate data to the cloud or back up data. Reverse synchronization: Select Yes to enable reverse synchronization. Reverse synchronization synchronizes metadata in the associated OSS bucket to the on-premises client. This feature is suitable for gateway disaster recovery, data restoration, and data sharing. Valid values: Yes: enables the reverse synchronization feature. If you enable the reverse synchronization feature, the gateway scans all objects in the OSS bucket. The scanning process is implemented by calling the OSS API. If a large number of objects exist in the OSS bucket, we recommend that you specify a time interval of at least 600 seconds to prevent low efficiency. No: disables the reverse synchronization feature. Reverse synchronization interval: Specify a time interval for reverse synchronization. Valid values: 15 to 36000. Unit: seconds. This parameter is available only when you set the Reverse synchronization parameter to Yes. Ignore deletion: If you select Yes, the data that is deleted from the on-premises cache disk is not deleted from the OSS bucket. Full data is stored in OSS. Synchronization delay: Specify a delay for synchronizing files from the on-premises cache disk to the OSS bucket. Default value: 5. Maximum value: 120. Unit: seconds. After you set this parameter, the gateway does not upload the files that you modified and closed until the specified amount of time is reached. This prevents file fragments generated in the OSS bucket due to frequent on-premises modifications. |

4. Click **OK**.

**What to do next**

After you create a share directory, you can access the NFS or SMB share directory. For more information, see Access an NFS share or Access an SMB share. This topic describes how to manage file gateways. You can follow the instructions provided in this topic to create, modify, and delete a file gateway.

**Prerequisites**

A virtual private cloud (VPC) and a vSwitch are created. For more information, see the "Create a VPC" and "Create a vSwitch" topics in **Apsara Stack**
**VPC User Guide**.
An Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance is created and used as a client, and the ECS instance is associated with the created VPC. For more information, see the "Create an instance" topic in **Apsara Stack ECS User Guide**.

**Create a gateway**

1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
3. If this is your first time using CSG, you must authorize CSG to access other Apsara Stack services based on your business requirements.
When you authorize CSG to access other Apsara Stack services, the service-linked role AliyunServiceRoleForHCSSGW is automatically created. The system attaches the AliyunServiceRolePolicyForHCSSGW policy to this service-linked role. In this case, CSG can assume the service-linked role and access other Apsara Stack services, such as OSS, VPC, and ECS. CSG provides a mount protocol based on the granted permissions to manage requests to OSS buckets, such as the requests to upload, download, or access data in OSS buckets. i. In the **Storage Gateway service authorization** message, read the authorization information and click **Authorize Now**. ii. Complete the authorization as prompted.
4. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, click **Create**.
5. In the **Create a gateway** dialog box, set the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Gateway name | Enter a name for the gateway instance. |
| Description | Enter a description for the gateway. |
| VPC | Select the VPC in which you want to deploy the gateway. Important You must select the VPC in which the ECS instance resides. |
| Virtual Switch | Select the vSwitch that you want to connect to the gateway. Important You must select the vSwitch to which the ECS instance is connected. |
| Gateway ECS specifications | After you select a vSwitch, you can view the specifications of the ECS instance, the number of vCPU cores, memory size, and internal bandwidth. |

6. Click **OK**.
After the gateway is created, the system automatically deploys and starts the gateway. It takes about 5 to 10 minutes to complete the process. The gateway enters the **Running** state if it is activated and deployed.

**More operations**

After a gateway is deployed, you can view the information about the gateway on the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, such as the service IP address, type, and status of the gateway. You can also perform the following operations on a gateway as needed.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| Modify a gateway | Modify the name or description of a gateway. 1. Find the gateway that you want to modify and clickE dit in the Operation column. 2. In the Edit Gateway dialog box, modify the gateway name or description. 3. Click OK. |
| Upgrade a gateway | By default, each gateway that you create is of the latest version. You can update a gateway only if a later gateway version is available. Find the gateway that you want to upgrade and clickU pgrade in the Operation column. |
| Restart a gateway | Find the gateway that you want to restart and clickR estart the Gateway in the Operation column. |
| Delete a gateway | Find the gateway that you want to delete and clickD elete in the Operation column. |

After a gateway is deployed, click the ID of the gateway on the **List of cloud storage gateways** page and perform operations on different tabs as needed. You can view the basic information about the gateway, including the name, ID, version, type, status, creation time, and activation time. Manage shares: On the **Share List** tab, you can create shares and restart Network File System (NFS) shares or Server Message Block (SMB) shares. Manage cache disks: On the **Cache** tab, you can view the information about the cache disks and scale out cache disks. Add SMB users: On the **SMB users** tab, you can create and delete SMB users.

**What to do next**

6. Click **OK**.

**Configure an NFS share**

If you select **NFS** as the protocol when you create a share, you can configure an NFS share. For example, you can specify the read/write users and read-only users.
1. On the **Share List** tab, find the share that you want to manage and click **Settings** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the **NFS share settings** panel, set the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| User Mapping | Specify the user mapping between the Network File System (NFS) client and the NFS server. none: NFS clients are not mapped to the nobody user on the NFS server. rootsquash: restricts the root user. NFS clients that use the root identity are mapped to the nobody user on the NFS server. _ allsquash: restricts all users. NFS clients are mapped to the nobody user on the NFS server regardless of the identity that the _ client uses. allanonymous: restricts all users. NFS clients are mapped to the anonymous user on the NFS server regardless of the identity that _ the client uses. |
| List of read/write clients | Enter the IP addresses or CIDR blocks of the NFS share that allow read and write access. Examples: 192.168.10.10 and 192.168.0.0/24. You can enter multiple IP addresses or CIDR blocks. |
| Read-only client list | Enter the IP addresses or CIDR blocks of the clients that can only read data from the NFS share. Examples: 192.168.10.10 and 192.168.0.0/24. You can enter multiple IP addresses or CIDR blocks. |
| Write speed limit | Specify the maximum write speed. Valid values: 0 to 1280. Unit: MB/s. The default value is 0, which specifies that the write speed is unlimited. |
| Upload speed limit | Specify the maximum upload speed. Valid values: 0 to 1280. Unit: MB/s. The default value is 0, which specifies that the upload speed is unlimited. Note If you limit the write speed and upload speed, make sure that the upload speed limit is not smaller than the write speed limit. |

3. Click **OK**.

**Configure an SMB share**

If you select **SMB** as the protocol when you create a share, you can configure an SMB share. For example, you can specify the read/write users and read-only users.
1. On the **Share List** tab, find the share that you want to manage and click **Settings** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the **SMB share settings** panel, set the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | description |
|---|---|
| Browsable | Specifies whether the SMB share can be discovered by network neighbors. Valid values: Yes: The SMB share can be discovered by network neighbors. No: The SMB share cannot be discovered by network neighbors. |
| Read and write users | Select the users who are allowed to read and write data from and to the SMB share. |
| Read-only users | Select the users who are allowed to only read data from the SMB share. Note If you grant both the read-only and read/write permissions to a user, the read-only permission takes effect. |
| Write speed limit | Specify the maximum write speed. Valid values: 0 to 1280. Unit: MB/s. The default value is 0, which specifies that the write speed is unlimited. |
| Upload speed limit | Specify the maximum upload speed. Valid values: 0 to 1280. Unit: MB/s. The default value is 0, which specifies that the upload speed is unlimited. Note If you limit the write speed and upload speed, make sure that the upload speed limit is not smaller than the write speed limit. |

3. Click **OK**.

**What to do next**

On the **Share List** page, perform operations based on your business requirements.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| Modify advanced settings | Modify advanced settings, such as reverse synchronization and ignore deletion. 1. Find the share that you want to modify and clickA dvanced Settings in the Operation column. 2. In the Advanced settings panel, configure the parameters. For more information about the parameters, see the Create a share section in this topic. 3. Click OK. |
| Delete a share | Find the share that you want to delete and clickD elete in the Operation column. When you delete a share, you can turn on Force delete as needed. Note This operation does not delete the data stored in the associated OSS bucket. This operation does not release the attached cache disk. If you create another share by using the cache disk, you must attach the cache disk and an OSS bucket to the share. |
| Restart NFS shares | Click Restart NFS share to restart all NFS shares that are connected to the current gateway. |
| Restart SMB shares | Click Restart SMB share to restart all SMB shares that are connected to the current gateway. |
| Hide tasks | Click Hide tasks below the share list to hide the tasks displayed at the bottom of the page. After the tasks are hidden, you can click Show tasks to display the task list. |
| View the upload and download queues | Find the share whose upload and download queues you want to view, and click the plus sign (+) next to the share name to view the upload and download queues. If the number of objects in the upload queue is not 0, one or more objects are waiting to be uploaded to the associated OSS bucket. If the number of objects in the download queue is not 0, one or more objects are waiting to be downloaded. If the numbers of objects in the upload and download queues are both 0, data has been synchronized between the gateway and the OSS bucket. |

This topic describes how to manage cache disks. You can scale up or delete cache disks.

**Prerequisites**

A share is created. For more information, see Create a share.

**Background information**

Each share of a file gateway is associated with a unique cache disk. To create multiple shares, you need to add an equal number of cache disks. By using a cache disk, you can upload data from a share to an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket or download data from an OSS bucket to a local device.

**Scale up a cache disk**

**Important**

If you scale up a cache disk, the share to which the cache disk is attached may be unavailable for about 5 minutes. After the cache disk is scaled up, the share is automatically recovered. You can only scale up disks. Scale-down is not supported. If a cache disk runs out of space, you can scale up the cache disk.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
3. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, find the gateway for which you want to create an SMB user and click the ID of the gateway.
4. On the **Cache** tab, find the cache that you want to scale up and click **Extended cache** in the **Operation** column.
5. In the **Extended cache** dialog box, set the cache disk size.
Valid values: 100 to 4096. Unit: GiB.
6. Click **OK**.

**Delete a cache disk**

You can delete a cache disk only if the cache disk is attached to no share.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
3. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, find the gateway for which you want to create an SMB user and click the ID of the gateway.
4. On the **Cache** tab, find the cache disk that you want to delete and click **Delete cache** in the **Operation** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
This topic describes how to create a Server Message Block (SMB) user. SMB users can access SMB shares.
1. Log in to the OSS console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
3. On the **List of cloud storage gateways** page, find the gateway for which you want to create an SMB user and click the ID of the gateway.
4. On the **SMB users** page, click **Create User** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Add SMB users** dialog box, enter a username and a password for the SMB user.
6. Click **OK**.
To delete the SMB user, click **Delete** in the **Operation** column. Before you delete an SMB user, make sure that the user is removed from the read/write and read-only permission lists of all shares. This is to prevent permission exceptions. This topic describes how to access a Network File System (NFS) share from a Linux Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance.

**Prerequisites**

A share is created. For more information, see Create a share.

**Important**

You can mount up to eight NFS or Server Message Block (SMB) shares to a gateway.

**Manually mount an NFS share**

1. Log in to the ECS console. For more information, see the "Connect to an instance" topic in **ECS User Guide**.
2. Connect to your Linux ECS instance. For more information, see the "Connect to an instance" topic in **ECS User Guide**.
3. On the ECS instance, run the following command to mount an NFS share to a local directory of the client:

```
mount.nfs 192.168.0.0:/shares local-directory
```

Command description: `192.168.0.0:/shares` is the mount target, which consists of the IPv4 address of the gateway and the share name. Replace them with your actual information. To view the mount target of the gateway, go to the **Share List** tab of the gateway. `local-directory` is the local directory of the client. You must specify a directory that allows read and write operations. You cannot specify a directory that does not exist.
4. Run the **df -h** command to query the mount result.
If the output is similar to the following information, the NFS share is mounted. After the NFS share is mounted, you can view the capacity of the file system that is managed by the NFS share. After an NFS share is mounted, you can access the NFS share in the same way as you access a local directory. If you have write permissions on the NFS share, you can write data to the NFS share. If you have read-only permissions on the NFS share, you can only read data from the NFS share. A share of a gateway is synchronized with the Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket associated with the share. When you manage a share, the changes to the share are also applied to the associated OSS bucket.

**Enable automatic mounting of an NFS share**

When you restart the ECS instance on which an NFS file system is mounted, the mount information about the file system may be lost. To prevent this issue, you can modify the /etc/fstab or /etc/rc.local configuration file on the Linux ECS instance to enable automatic mounting at system startup for the NFS file system. We recommend that you use the /etc/fstab file. Before you configure a share to be automatically mounted, make sure that you have manually mounted the share. This prevents automatic mount failures after an ECS instance restart.
1. Open the configuration file and add the mount configurations.
Method 1 (recommended): Open the /etc/fstab configuration file and add the mount configurations. If your client runs CentOS 6, perform the following steps first: a. Run the `chkconfig netfs on` command to enable NetFS startup upon system boot. b. Open the /etc/netconfig file and comment out inet6-related information. To use NFSv4 to mount the file system, add the following command:

```
192.168.0.0:/shares local-directory nfs defaults 0 0
```

To use NFSv3 to mount the file system, add the following command:

```
192.168.0.0:/shares local-directory nfs vers=3.0 defaults 0 0
```

Method 2: Open the /etc/rc.local configuration file and add the mount configurations. Before you modify the /etc/rc.local file, make sure that you have execute permissions on the /etc/rc.local and /etc/rc.d/rc.local files. For example, in CentOS 7.x, execute permissions are not granted by default. Before you modify the /etc/rc.local file, grant execute permissions on the files to the account that you use to log on to the ECS instance. To use NFSv4 to mount the file system, add the following command:

```python
sudo mount.nfs 192.168.0.0:/shares local-directory
```

To use NFSv3 to mount the file system, add the following command:

```python
sudo mount -t nfs -o vers=3,proto=tcp,nolock 192.168.0.0:/shares local-directory
```

Command description: `192.168.0.0:/shares` is the mount target, which consists of the IPv4 address of the gateway and the share name. Replace them with your actual information. To view the mount target of the gateway, go to the **Share List** tab of the gateway. `local-directory` is the local directory of the client. You must specify a directory that allows read and write operations. You cannot specify a directory that does not exist.
2. Run the **reboot** command to restart the ECS instance.

## 3 EBS

### 3.1 What is EBS?

Elastic Block Storage (EBS) is a persistent random block storage service that provides low latency and high reliability and is designed for Elastic Compute Service (ECS). EBS provides devices based on a distributed storage architecture. The EBS console provides an all-in-one solution for cloud-based EBS management. You can use the EBS console to manage enterprise-level features and other features, such as storage resource management, monitoring, performance analysis, disaster recovery, and alerting. As a centralized service platform for the entire EBS infrastructure, the EBS console informs you of resources in the cloud to best support business and optimize costs by analyzing long-term data trends. EBS supports high elasticity. The performance and capacity of the entire cluster can linearly scale with the cluster size. You can expand the cluster capacity to hundreds of thousands of nodes and store exabytes of data in a region.

**Block storage**

Block storage devices offer high performance and reduced latency. You can partition and format these devices and create file systems on the devices to meet the data storage requirements of your business. EBS provides ECS instances with block-level storage that features low latency, persistence, and high reliability. EBS devices adopt the Erasure Coding (EC) mechanism to ensure data durability for ECS instances and support the triplicate storage mode. You can create, release, and resize EBS devices based on your business requirements. You can resize EBS devices, including system disks and data disks, without interrupting your business. When you resize an EBS device, you do not need to stop the ECS instance to which the EBS device is attached or detach the EBS device from the ECS instance.

**Cloud disk**

Cloud disks are block-level EBS devices that use the EC mechanism and support the triplicate storage mode.

**Snapshot**

A snapshot is a point-in-time backup of a cloud disk and is used to back up or restore the cloud disk. The async replication feature can asynchronously replicate data from a primary disk to a secondary disk in another zone on the same cloud or on another cloud at the scheduled time. In async replication, the data on the primary disk may be inconsistent with that on the secondary disk.

**EC**

EC involves the following two concepts: Data fragments (n): Data is divided into n data fragments. Parity fragments (m): m parity fragments are computed from the n data fragments. The n data fragments and m parity fragments that reside on different servers compose an EC group. If the number of lost fragments is less than or equal to m, the lost fragments can be restored based on the EC algorithm. You can configure the values of n and m. In most cases of Apsara Stack, the value of n is set to 8, the value of m is set to 3, and 14 or more servers are used. EBS provides cloud disks.

**Cloud disk**

Cloud disks are block-level storage devices provided by Apsara Stack for ECS instances. Cloud disks can be classified based on their performance or purposes. Shared disks are discontinued.

**Performance-based classification**

Cloud disks are classified by performance into premium performance disks, standard performance disks, ultra disks, and standard SSDs.

**Important**

If you deploy an EBS cluster of the latest version, you can use only premium performance disks and standard performance disks. If you update an EBS cluster from an earlier version to the latest version, you can continue to use ultra disks and standard SSDs in addition to newly supported premium performance disks and standard performance disks. Standard performance disks and premium performance disks are ideal for online transaction processing (OLTP) databases and NoSQL databases. Premium performance disks provide up to 25,000 random IOPS for ECS instances. Ultra disks are ideal for medium I/O load scenarios and provide up to 3,000 random IOPS for ECS instances. Standard SSDs are ideal for I/O-intensive applications and feature stable and high random IOPS performance. The following table compares the performance of different cloud disks.

| Comparison item | Premium performance disk | Standard performance disk | Standard SSD | Ultra disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Maximum capacity per disk (GiB) | 131,072​ GiB | 32768 GiB | 32768 GiB | 32768 GiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maximum IOPS | 25000 | 5000 | 25000 | 5000 |
| Maximum throughput (MB/s) | 300 MB/s | 140 MB/s | 300 MB/s | 140 MB/s |
| Formula for calculating the IOPS per disk | min(1,800 + 30 × Capacity, 25,000) | min(1,800 + 8 × Capacity, 5,000) | min(1,800 + 30 × Capacity, 25,000) | min(1,800 + 8 × Capacity, 5,000) |
| Formula for calculating the throughput per disk | min(120 + 0.5 × Capacity, 300) MB/s | min(100 + 0.15 × Capacity, 140) MB/s | min(120 + 0.5 × Capacity, 300) MB/s | min(100 + 0.15 × Capacity, 140) MB/s |
| Type name in API operations | cloudpperf _ | cloudsperf _ | cloudssd _ | cloudefficiency _ |
| Scenarios | OLTP databases: relational databases, such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server databases NoSQL databases: non-relational databases, such as MongoDB, HBase, and Cassandra databases Elasticsearch distributed logs: Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana (ELK) log analysis |   | Small and medium-sized development and test applications that require high data reliability | Development and test applications System disks |

**Purpose-based classification**

Cloud disks are classified into system disks and data disks based on their purposes. System disks are created and released along with the ECS instances to which they are attached and have the same lifecycle as the instances. Shared access is not allowed for system disks. Data disks can be separately created or created along with ECS instances. Shared access is not allowed for data disks. A data disk created together with an ECS instance has the same lifecycle as the instance and is released along with the instance. A data disk that is separately created can be separately released or released along with the ECS instance to which it is attached. The capacity of a data disk is determined by the disk type. Elastic Block Storage (EBS) provides various features such as read/write stability, backup, data erasure mechanism, data encryption, elastic storage, and disaster recovery.

**Read/write stability**

| Erasure coding (EC) is an encoding technology that improves data reliability and fault tolerance. Compared with triplicate storage, EC can implement |   |
|---|---|
| high data reliability with lower data redundancy and ensure data stability during read and write operations. | By default, EBS clusters use EC to ensure |

data reliability and consistency. You can configure EC. For more information, see EC. If you want to store business data as multiple replicas in an EBS cluster in the same zone, set the replica policy of the cluster to triplicate storage. For more information, see Triplicate storage.

**Backup**

To improve the security of your business data, you can periodically create snapshots to provide data backup capabilities for disks. This ensures that information such as logs and customer transactions is backed up for future use. For more information, see Overview. You can use automatic snapshot policies to improve data security and tolerance against operation faults. Automatic snapshot policies can take effect on system disks and data disks to periodically create snapshots for the disks. To simultaneously create snapshots for multiple disks on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, you can create a snapshot-consistent group by adding the disks. If a business system involves multiple disks, you can create a snapshot-consistent group to ensure a consistent write order and the crash consistency of business system data.

**Data erasure mechanism**

When you delete data, the data is completely erased from the distributed block storage system and can no longer be accessed by other users. The following mechanisms ensure that deleted data is completely erased: The storage system performs sequential writes to append data to existing files at the underlying layer of disks. This mechanism fully utilizes highbandwidth and low-latency sequential writes to physical disks. If you delete a logical space from a disk after data is appended at the underlying layer of the disk, the delete operation is recorded as metadata. The storage system returns only zeros for all requests of reading data from the logical space. Similarly, when you overwrite data that is stored in the logical space of a disk, the storage system does not immediately overwrite the data in the corresponding physical space. Instead, the storage system modifies the mapping between the logical space and the physical space to ensure that the overwritten data is no longer readable. Data fragments caused by delete or overwrite operations are forcibly and permanently deleted from the underlying physical disks. When a block storage device (disk) is released, the storage system immediately destroys the metadata of the device to ensure that the data is no longer accessible. At the same time, the physical storage space of the device is recycled. The physical storage space must be cleared before the storage space is re-assigned. Before data is written to a new disk, the system returns only zeros for all read requests.

**Data encryption**

If your applications are data-sensitive, we recommend that you encrypt your storage devices. Disks and their snapshots are encrypted by using keys based on the industry-standard AES-256 algorithm. Data is automatically encrypted when it is transmitted from ECS instances to disks and then decrypted when it is read. For more information, see Disk encryption.

**Elastic storage**

You can resize disks to meet increasing storage requirements as your business and application data grow. For more information, see EBS device resizing. Async replication is a feature that protects data across zones within the same cloud or across clouds based on the data replication capability of EBS. This feature can asynchronously replicate data from a disk to another disk in another zone in the same cloud or in another cloud, implementing isaster recovery across zones in the same cloud or across clouds. You can use this feature to implement disaster recovery for critical business to protect data in your databases and improve business continuity. For more information, see Disk disaster recovery. If a replication pair and a replication pair-consistent group have the same primary region (production region), primary zone (production zone), secondary region (disaster recovery region), and secondary zone (disaster recovery zone), the replication pair and replication pair-consistent group replicate data in the same direction. You can add replication pairs that replicate data between the production site and disaster recovery site in the same direction as a replication pair-consistent group to the group so that you can manage these replication pairs as a batch by using the group. Apsara Distributed File System provides stable, efficient, and reliable data access to Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances.

**Chunk**

When ECS users perform read and write operations on virtual disks, the operations are translated into processes on the files stored in Apsara Stack data storage system. Apsara Stack uses a flat design in which a linear address space is divided into slices called chunks. Each chunk is replicated into three copies. Each copy is stored on a different node in the cluster, which ensures data reliability. Figure 1. Triplicate backup

**How triplicate technology works**

Triplicate storage involves three types of key component: master, chunk server, and client. Each write operation performed by an ECS user is converted into an operation for the client to execute by performing the following steps:
1. The client receives a write request and determines the chunk that corresponds to the write operation.
2. The client queries the master to find the chunk servers where the three copies of the chunk are stored.
3. The client sends write requests to the chunk servers returned from the master.
4. If the write operation succeeds on all of the three chunk copies, the client returns a success. If one of the write operations fails, the client returns a
failure. The distribution policy of the master takes factors of all chunk servers in the cluster into account, such as chunk server disk usage, chunk server distribution across racks, power distribution conditions, and machine workloads The master ensures that the three copies of a chunk are distributed on different chunk servers in different racks. This effectively prevents a single point of failure caused by the failure of a chunk server or rack.

**Data protection mechanism**

When a data node is damaged or disk faults occur on a data node, the number of valid copies of some chunks within the cluster may become less than three. In this case, the master replicates data between chunk servers to make sure that each chunk in the cluster has three valid replicas. Figure 2. Automatic replication All operations performed by users on data of disks are synchronized across the three chunk copies at the underlying layer. Operations that are synchronized include adding, modifying, and deleting data. This mode ensures the reliability and consistency of user data. To prevent data losses caused by viruses, accidental deletion, or malicious attacks, we recommend that you use other protection methods such as data backup and snapshots. Implement all appropriate measures to ensure the security and availability of your data.

**3.1.1.3. EC**

Erasure coding (EC) can improve storage reliability. Compared to triplicate storage, EC can provide higher data reliability at lower data redundancy levels.

**What is EC?**

EC involves the following concepts: Data fragments (n): Data is divided into n data fragments. Parity fragments (m): m parity fragments are computed from the n data fragments. The n data fragments and m parity fragments that reside on different servers compose an EC group. If the number of lost fragments is less than or equal to m, the lost fragments can be restored based on the EC algorithm. You can configure the values of n and m. In most cases of Apsara Stack, the value of n is set to 8, the value of m is set to 3, and the number of servers is no less than 14.

**Comparison between EC and triplicate storage**

Compared to triplicate storage, EC is a better solution in terms of storage usage and data reliability.

| Item | EC | Triplicate storage |
|---|---|---|
| Storage usage | n/(n + m) : When n is 8 and m is 3, the storage usage is calculated based on the following formula: 8/(8 + 3) = 72.7%. | 1/3 = 33.3% |
| Reliability | Allows up to m fragments to be lost. Failures on up to m servers are allowed in the worst case. For example, if n is 8 and m is 3, failures on up to three servers are allowed. | Allows up to two replicas to be lost. Failures on up to two servers are allowed in the worst case. |

Disk encryption provides a simple and secure way to encrypt newly created disks. You can use disk encryption without building, maintaining, or securing your own key management infrastructure. It requires no changes to your applications or workflows, and the encryption is transparent to your services. Disk encryption encrypts the following types of data: Data on encrypted disks. Data transmitted between disks and instances. Data within the instance's operating system is not encrypted. All snapshots created from an encrypted disk (encrypted snapshots). Data transmitted from an ECS instance to a disk is encrypted on the physical machine that hosts the instance. Disk encryption is available for all disk types in Apsara Stack, including ESSD, basic disk, ultra disk, and standard SSD.
