You can clone a disk to quickly create a replica that is identical to the existing disk. This allows you to back up data, migrate the system environment, or create a test environment with ease to ensure business continuity and data security.

**Prerequisites**

A disk is in the **Running** or **Available** state. The disk in the **Available** state was attached to an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance and then detached from the ECS instance. You cannot clone a disk across regions.

**Billing**

The replica uses the pay-as-you-go billing method. Bills are generated only after the administrator configures billing rules in the operation center. For more information about billing rules, see the topics under **Operations > Pricing > Manage billing configurations** in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User Guide in Apsara Stack Documentation Center.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. On the Disks page, find the disk that you want to clone, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Clone Disk**.
5. In the **Clone Disk** dialog box, enter a value in the **Destination Disk Quantity** field in the Destination Disk Settings step and click **Next**.
6. In the Configuration Preview step, preview the ID and type of the disk to be cloned, as well as the size, region, and zone of the replicas, and then click
**Submit**.
7. View the information about the replicas in the destination region.
This process is implemented by CloudOps Orchestration Service (OOS). You can log on to the OOS console to view the progress of the clone operation. For more information about how to log on to the OOS console, see **Log on to the OOS console** in **OOS User Guide** in the Apsara Stack Documentation Center. If you have created a snapshot for a disk, you can use the rollback feature to restore the data of the disk to a specific point in time. The disk rollback operation is irreversible. After the disk is rolled back, the data stored on the disk before the operation is performed cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**Prerequisites**

A snapshot of the disk to be rolled back is created, and no other snapshot is being created for the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The disk is not released. The instance to which the disk belongs is in the **Stopped** state.
1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the snapshot that you want to use to roll back the specified disk and click **Roll Back Disk** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **Roll Back Disk**.

**What to do next**

After a disk is rolled back, the host configuration file and the configurations, such as the hostname, SSH key pair, password, network, system source, and clock source, are initialized. You must reconfigure the settings. If you resized a disk after you created a snapshot for the disk, the size of the disk is also rolled back after you roll back the disk. To make the disk revert to the size before the rollback, you must log on to the instance to resize the file system. For more information, see Resize a disk. This topic describes how to re-initialize a system disk. After a system disk is re-initialized, the system disk is restored to the state at the time when it was created.

**Prerequisites**

The disk is in the **Running** state. The Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance to which the system disk is attached is in the **Stopped** state. After a disk is re-initialized, the data stored on the disk is lost and cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when you perform this operation. If you need the data stored on the system disk, we recommend that you back up the disk data or create snapshots before you re-initialize the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot.

**Background information**

The result of disk re-initialization depends on the disk type and how the disk was created. If a system disk is attached to an ECS instance, you can re-initialize the system disk to restore it to the state at the time when it was created. The following section describes the changes of a system disk after it is re-initialized: The system disk is restored to the state when it was created.

**Warning**

When the system disk is re-initialized, all data stored on the disk is deleted. We recommend that you create snapshots to back up data before you re-initialize the disk. If an automatic snapshot policy was applied to the system disk, the policy remains in effect for the disk. The IP addresses and disk IDs of the instance remain unchanged. The snapshots of the system disk are retained. You can use these snapshots to roll back the disk. For more information, see Roll back a disk by using a snapshot.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the system disk that you want to re-initialize, and click **Re-initialize Disk** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Re-initialize Disk** dialog box, configure the parameters as required. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Password | Reset the password used to log on to the instance. You can use the original password or specify a new password. |
| Confirm Password |   |
| Instance Startup Policy | If you select Start Instance After Re-initializing Disk, the instance automatically starts after you re-initialize the system disk. |

6. Click **OK**.

**Results**

When the disk is being re-initialized, the disk is in the **Initializing** state. After the disk is re-initialized, it enters the **Running** state.

**What to do next**

If data disks are attached to a Linux instance before its system disk is re-initialized, you must re-create mount targets for the partitions of the data disks and mount file systems to these partitions. After you re-initialize the system disk of a Linux instance, data stored on the data disks attached to the instance remains unchanged, but the attachment information of the data disks is lost. You must re-create the mount targets for the data disk partitions and mount file systems to the data disk partitions. After the system disk is re-initialized, you must redeploy applications and reconfigure parameters on the disk to restore your business at the earliest opportunity. If you created a snapshot for the system disk before the system disk is re-initialized, you can use the snapshot to create a data disk and attach the data disk to the instance to obtain data that was originally stored on the system disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. If a data disk is attached to an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, you can re-initialize the disk to restore it to the state at the time when it was created.

**Prerequisites**

Snapshots are created for the data disk that you want to re-initialize. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The data disk is attached to an ECS instance. For more information, see Attach disks. The ECS instance is in the **Stopped** state. For a Linux instance, if you create an empty data disk and add a command in the /etc/fstab file to mount partitions of the data disk on system startup, the command is not executed and the instance cannot start as expected after you re-initialize the data disk. We recommend that you comment out the command in the /etc/fstab file. To do so, perform the following steps: i. Connect to the instance. For more information, see the "Connect to an instance" section in **ECS User Guide**. ii. Run the `vim /etc/fstab` command. iii. Press the `I` key to enter Insert mode. iv. Find each command that is used to mount a partition of the data disk and add a number sign (`#`) to comment out the command, as shown in the following example:

| # /dev/vdb1 /InitTest ext3 defaults 0 0 |   |   |   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Note /dev/vdb1 is a data disk partition and /InitTest is a mount target used in this example. Replace /dev/vdb1 and /mnt with actual values. |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| Press the | Esc | key to exit Insert mode and then enter | :wq | to s | ave | the file and exit. |

**Background information**

After you re-initialize a data disk, the state of the disk varies based on the initial state of the disk and the operating system that the ECS instance runs. The data disk is restored to the initial state when the disk was created. If the data disk was initially an empty disk, the disk becomes an empty disk. If the data disk was created from a snapshot, the disk is restored to the initial state when the disk was created from the snapshot. For a Windows instance, after you re-initialize a data disk, the data disk is ready for use without the need for additional operations regardless of its original state. For a Linux instance: If you re-initialize a data disk that was created from a snapshot, the disk is restored to the initial state when the disk was created from the snapshot. You do not need to remount the partitions of the disk. However, all data generated after the disk was created is lost. If you re-initialize a data disk that was initially an empty disk, all data and file systems on the disk are lost. You must reformat and partition the data disk and then remount the partitions of the disk.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the data disk that you want to re-initialize, and click **Re-initialize Disk** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Re-initialize Disk** dialog box, click **OK**.

**What to do next**

For a Linux instance, if the data disk was created as an empty disk, you must format the data disk after you re-initialize it. For more information, see Format a data disk on a Linux instance. After the data disk is re-initialized, you must redeploy applications and reconfigure parameters on the disk to restore your business at the earliest opportunity. Elastic Block Storage (EBS) offers different categories of disks to meet storage performance requirements in various scenarios. You can change the categories of your disks as required.

**Background information**

Before you change the category of a disk, take note of the following items: The change operations on disk categories described in the following table are supported.

| Disk category | Supported change |
|---|---|
| Ultra disk | You can convert ultra disks into standard SSDs, standard performance disks, or premium performance disks. |
| Standard SSD | You can convert standard SSDs into ultra disks, standard performance disks, or premium performance disks. |
| Premium performance disk | You can convert premium performance disks only into standard performance disks. |
| Standard performance disk | You can convert standard performance disks only into premium performance disks. |

When you change the category of a disk, the performance of the disk may vary. We recommend that you change the categories of your disks during off-peak hours. It may take hours to change the category of a disk. In rare cases, the change operation may fail due to resource issues. If the change operation fails, try again later.

| Phase | Limit |
|---|---|
| Before the disk category change | Before you change the category of a disk, make sure that the following requirements are met: You can concurrently run at most five disk category change tasks within the same region and account. You cannot change the category of a disk attached to an instance whose configurations are being changed. |
| During the disk category change | The following limits apply when the category of a disk is being changed: You cannot cancel the disk category change task after it is initiated. You cannot create a snapshot for the disk. You cannot resize the disk. You cannot re-initialize the disk. You cannot roll back the disk by using a snapshot. You cannot attach the disk to an instance or detach it from an instance. If the disk is a system disk, you cannot change the operating system of the instance. |
| After the disk category change | A disk can have its category changed only once within seven days. |

1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the disk whose category you want to change, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then click **Change Disk Category**.
5. Optional. Select a service catalog and click **OK**.
Service catalogs are used to manage the specifications of specific services in an enterprise or organization. This option is available only if a service catalog is configured and activated for the current organization or user in service management. For more information about service management, see the **Service catalogs** topic in **Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User Guide** .
6. In the **Change Disk Category** dialog box, select a disk category from the **New Disk Category** drop-down list.
7. Click **OK** to submit the disk category change task. When the task is in progress, you can click **View Task** in the **Status** column to go to the
Asynchronous Tasks page and view the status and progress of the task. After the task is completed, you can choose **Maintenance & Monitoring > Asynchronous Tasks** in the left-side navigation pane to view information about historical tasks.

**Results**

On the **Disks** page, find the disk for which you have changed the category and view its category. The new category is displayed. If a data disk is no longer needed by an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, you can detach the disk from the instance. You can also detach a data disk from an instance and then attach the disk to another instance within the same zone. This topic describes how to detach a data disk.

**Prerequisites**

Before you detach a data disk, make sure that the following conditions are met: The disk is attached to an instance and **Running** is displayed in the **Status** column that corresponds to the disk in the ECS console. To prevent data loss and ensure data integrity, we recommend that you stop read and write operations on the data disk before you detach the disk.

**Background information**

To detach a data disk, perform the following steps. Local disks that are used as data disks cannot be detached.
1. If file systems are mounted to the partitions of the data disk, detach the data disk from within the operating system of the instance to which the data
disk is attached. For more information, see the Step 1: Detach the data disk from within the operating system of the associated ECS instance section of this topic.
2. On the Disks page, detach the data disk.
For more information, see the Step 2: Detach the data disk on the Disks page section of this topic.

**Step 1: Detach the data disk from within the operating system of the associated instance**

If the data disk is partitioned and file systems on the disk are mounted, perform the following operations to detach the data disk from within the operating system of the ECS instance to which the disk is attached.

**For a Linux instance, perform the following steps:**

1. Connect to the Linux instance.
For more information, see the "Connect to an instance" section in **ECS User Guide**.
2. Run the following command to view the mount information of the data disk:

```
df -h
```

A command output similar to the following one is displayed. In this example, the /dev/vdb1 partition of the data disk is used. In actual scenarios, look up the command output for the data disk partitions whose mount information you want to view.
3. Run the umount command to unmount the file systems of the data disk partitions.
For example, you can run the following command to unmount the file system of the /dev/vdb1 partition:

```
umount /dev/vdb1
```

4. Run the following command to view the UUIDs of the data disk partitions:

```
blkid
```

The following sample command output indicates the UUID of the /dev/vdb1 partition of the data disk.
5. Run the following command to check whether the /etc/fstab file contains the automatic mounting configurations of the file systems in the data disk
partitions:

```
cat /etc/fstab
```

Find the UUID obtained in the previous step in the command output. The file system mounted to the /dev/vdb1 partition is configured in /etc/fstab, as shown in the following figure.
6. Delete the automatic mounting configurations of the file systems in the data disk partitions from /etc/fstab.
If you do not delete the automatic mounting configurations of the file systems in the data disk partitions from /etc/fstab, the ECS instance cannot be restarted after you detach the data disk from the instance. i. Run the following command to modify the /etc/fstab file:

| vim /etc/fstab |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Press the | I | key to enter Insert mode. |

iii. Delete or comment out the automatic mounting configurations of the file systems in the data disk partitions. For example, you can add a number sign ( `#` ) before a line that contains automatic mounting configuration to comment out the configuration, as shown in the following figure. iv. Press the Esc key, enter `:wq` , and then press the Enter key to save and close the file.

**For a Windows instance, perform the following steps:**

In this example, Windows Server 2012 R2 is used.
1. Connect to the Windows instance.
For more information, see the "Connect to an instance" section in **ECS User Guide**.
2. On the Windows Server desktop, click the **Server Manager** icon in the lower-left corner.
3. In the upper-right corner of the **Server Manager** window, choose **Tools > Computer Management**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Computer Management (Local) > Storage > Disk Management**.
5. Right-click the disk that you want to detach and select **Offline**.

**Step 2: Detach the data disk on the Disks page**

You can detach disks from instances on the Disks or ECS Instances page in the ECS console. This section describes how to detach a data disk on the Disks page.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the disk that you want to detach, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Detach**.
5. In the message that appears, click **Detach**.
Alternatively, you can go to the Instance Details page of the associated instance and detach the data disk from the instance on the **Disks** tab.

**Results**

After you detach a data disk, you can choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks** in the left-side navigation pane of the ECS console and then find the disk on the Disks page. If **Available** is displayed in the **Status** column, the disk is detached from the original instance.

**What to do next**

You can attach the data disk to another instance within the same zone. For more information, see Attach disks. If you no longer need the data disk that you detached, you can back up data stored on the disk and then release the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot and Release a data disk. You can manually release disks that are no longer needed. When a disk is released, all data stored on the disk is deleted. This topic describes how to release a data disk on the Disks page in the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) console.

**Prerequisites**

A snapshot is created for the disk that you want to release to back up the data stored on the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The data disk is in the **Available** state. If the data disk is attached to an instance, you must detach the disk from the instance before you can release the disk. For more information, see Detach a data disk.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the data disk that you want to release, click the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then click **Release**.
5. Release a disk.
If a service whose **Resources** value is **ECS Disk** exists on the Service Management page, select **Move to Recycle Bin** in the dialog box that appears and click **Confirm Order**. If a service whose **Resources** value is **ECS Disk** does not exist on the Service Management page, select **Move to Recycle Bin** in the dialog box that appears and click **Submit**.

**Verify the result**

Whether **Move to Recycle Bin** is selected determines the data disk release result: If you do not select **Move to Recycle Bin**, the data disk is deleted. If you select **Move to Recycle Bin**, the status of the data disk changes to **Soft Deletion - Moved to Recycle Bin** and the `acs:ecs:disk:preRelease` tag is added to the data disk. In this case, you can only restore the disk from the recycle bin or permanently delete the disk. You cannot perform the following operations on the disk: Mount the disk, expand the disk, or change the type of the disk. Modify the attributes of the disk. Clone the disk. Reset or initialize the disk. Associate the disk with a snapshot policy, create snapshots of the disk, or create snapshot-consistent groups for the disk. When you release a data disk, you can move the disk to the recycle bin and specify the retention period of the disk. The retention period specifies how long resources are kept in the recycle bin. Within the retention period, you can restore the disk from the recycle bin. After the retention period ends, the disk will be permanently deleted and cannot be restored. This topic describes how to manage the recycle bin.

**Move a disk to the recycle bin**

**Prerequisites**

A snapshot is created for the disk that you want to release to back up the data stored on the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The data disk is in the **Available** state. If the data disk is attached to an instance, you must detach the disk from the instance before you can release the disk. For more information, see Detach a data disk.
1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
4. Find the data disk that you want to release, click the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then click **Release**.
5. In the dialog box that appears, turn on **Move to Recycle Bin** and specify the Retention Period parameter. Valid values: 1 hour to 364 days and 23
hours.
6. Click **Release**.

**Verify the result**

The status of the disk changes from **Available** to **Soft Deletion - Moved to Recycle Bin** .

**Restore the disk**

Before the retention period ends, you can restore the disk from the recycle bin.
1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Recycle Bin**. On the page that appears, click the **Disk Recycle Bin** tab.
4. Find the disk to be restored.
i. To restore a single disk, find the disk in the recycle bin and click **Restore** in the Actions column. In the message that appears, click **OK**. ii. To restore one or more disks at a time, select the disks and click **Restore** below the list. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Verify the result**

The status of the disk changes from **Soft Deletion - Moved to Recycle Bin** to **Available**. You can perform operations on the disk in the disk list.

**Permanently delete the disk**

Before the retention period ends, you can permanently delete the disk.

**Important**

After the disk is permanently deleted, it cannot be restored. Make sure that your business is not interrupted before you permanently delete the disk.
1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Recycle Bin**. Then, click the **Disk Recycle Bin** tab.
4. Find the disk that you want to delete.
i. To delete a single disk, click **Permanently Delete** in the Actions column of the disk. In the message that appears, click **Delete**. ii. To delete one or more disks at a time, select the disks that you want to delete, and then click **Permanently Delete** below the list. In the message that appears, click **Delete**.

**Verify the result**

After the disk is permanently deleted, the data in the disk is also deleted and cannot be restored.

### 3.5 Snapshots

You can use snapshots to back up data, restore Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances that were accidentally released, and create custom images. Before you roll back disks, modify critical system files, or change the operating system of an instance, you can create snapshots for disks to improve fault tolerance.

**Prerequisites**

The instance to which the disk is attached and for which you want to create a snapshot is in the **Running** or **Stopped** state. The disk is in the **Running** state.

**Background information**

You can create a maximum of 64 snapshots for each disk. Snapshots can be used in the following scenarios: Roll back the data of the disk for which a snapshot is created. For more information, see Roll back a disk by using a snapshot. Create a custom image from a snapshot. For more information, see Create a custom image from a snapshot.

**Important**

You cannot use a data disk snapshot to create custom images. Create a data disk from a data disk snapshot. To create a data disk from a data disk snapshot, set the Use Snapshot parameter to Yes and then specify a snapshot on the Create Disk page. For more information, see Create a disk. The size of the disk to be created is determined by the size of the specified snapshot and cannot be changed. When you re-initialize a data disk created from a snapshot, the data on the disk is restored to that of the snapshot used to create the disk. When you create a snapshot, take note of the following items: For each disk, the first snapshot is a full snapshot and subsequent snapshots are incremental snapshots. It takes longer to create the first snapshot. The amount of time it takes to create an incremental snapshot depends on the volume of data that has been changed since the last snapshot. The more data that has changed, the longer it takes. If you want to use a snapshot immediately after it is created, you can enable the instant access feature. We recommend that you create snapshots during off-peak hours. The size of a disk for which you want to create a snapshot cannot exceed 128 TiB.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Disks**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. On the Disks page, find the disk for which you want to create a snapshot and click **Create Snapshot** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Create Snapshot** dialog box, set the parameters and click **OK**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Snapshot Name | The name of the snapshot. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length. It must start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https://. It can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (), and hyphens (-). _ Note The name cannot start with auto because snapshots whose names start with auto are recognized as automatic snapshots. |

| Instant Access | After you create snapshots that have the instant access feature enabled, you can immediately use the snapshots to create or roll back disks. You can configure the Instant Access parameter only for premium performance disks. To enable the instant access feature when you create a snapshot for a premium performance disk, selectE nable Instant Access. |
|---|---|
| Snapshot Description | The description of the snapshot. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |

You can go to the Snapshots page to check the creation progress of the snapshot. For more information, see View snapshots. After the snapshot is created, 100% is displayed in the Progress column. You view the details of created snapshots, including the snapshot names, snapshot IDs, snapshot status, snapshot creation time, names of the source disks (disks from which the snapshots are created), IDs of the source disks, and types of the source disks. You can also view the details of the custom images and disks that are created from a snapshot.
1. Log on to the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Click the **Disk Snapshots** tab.
5. Select a field, such as **Snapshot ID**, from the drop-down list and enter a keyword in the search box. The snapshots that meet the filter condition are
displayed in the list. You can search for snapshots by using the **Automatic Identification**, **Snapshot Name**, **Snapshot ID**, **Disk ID**, **Creation Time**, or
**Filter by Tag** filter option.
Fuzzy search is supported for the **Snapshot Name**, **Snapshot ID**, or **Disk ID** filter option. You can specify multiple filter conditions to narrow down search results.
6. In the **Snapshot ID/Name** column, click the ID of a snapshot to go to the Snapshot Details page.

**View the snapshot details:**

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Basic Information | This section displays basic information about the snapshot, including the snapshot name, snapshot ID, snapshot status, snapshot creation progress, snapshot type, snapshot creation time, and Instance Access setting. |
| Disk Information | This section displays information about the disk from which the snapshot was created, including the disk name, disk ID, disk status, and disk type. |
| Relevant information | Images created from snapshots This tab displays information about the custom images that are created from the snapshot, including the IDs, names, status, and sharing scopes of the custom images. You can click the ID of a custom image in the custom image list to go to theE CS Image > Custom Image tab and view the details of the custom image. For more information, see the Images > Custom images > Find a custom image section in ECS User Guide. Disks Created from Snapshots This tab displays information about the disks that are created from the snapshot, including the IDs, names, status, categories, types, and encryption settings of the disks. You can click the ID of a disk in the disk list to go to theD isk Details tab and view the details of the disk. For more information, see Search for and view a disk. |

**View snapshot operation logs:**

Click the **Operation Log** tab to view the operation logs of a snapshot, including the operation name, operator, execution status, operation source (console call or API call), operation type, operation source IP address, and operation time. Select a field from the field drop-down list and enter a keyword in the search box. The snapshots that meet the filter condition are displayed in the list. You can also click **Operation Details** in the Operation column to view detailed operation logs. Operation logs can be retained for seven days. You can contact the administrator to change the retention period of operation logs on the Log Storage Settings page. To go to this page, click **Configurations > Log Storage Settings** in the left-side navigation pane. For more information, see the **Configuration center > Log dump settings** section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User Guide. If you use the log dump settings to extend the log retention period, the log data generated before the specified time is not dumped. For example, if you enable log dump at 15:50, the log data generated before this point in time is not dumped. You can use the snapshot sharing feature to share snapshots created in the current organization with other organizations. Members in these organizations can create disks based on the shared snapshots.

**Prerequisites**

Snapshots are created for the relevant disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot.

**Background information**

Snapshots can be shared only among level-1 organizations. A single snapshot can be shared with up to 10 organizations at a time. A single snapshot can be shared with up to 64 organizations in total. Shared snapshots cannot be used to create custom images. Snapshots shared by an organization cannot be shared by the organization that accepts the snapshots. Snapshots with the instant access feature enabled cannot be shared. Limits on encrypted snapshots: To share snapshots that are encrypted by using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-256, you must attach a Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has permissions on the relevant customer master key (CMK) managed by Key Management Service (KMS) to the organization to which you want to share the snapshots. For more information, see the RAM role-based authorization for encrypted snapshots section of this topic. Snapshots encrypted by using default keys cannot be shared. Snapshots encrypted by using ShangMi 4 (SM4) cannot be shared. When you use a shared encrypted snapshot to create disks, you must specify a different encryption key for the disks instead of using the encryption key of the snapshot. Before you can delete a shared snapshot, you must unshare the snapshot. For more information, see the Unshare a snapshot section of this topic. After a snapshot is unshared or the shared source snapshot is deleted, an organization that accepted the shared snapshot cannot re-initialize a data disk created from the snapshot.

**Share a snapshot**

1. Log on to the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. On the **Disk Snapshots** tab, find the snapshot that you want to share and click **Share Snapshot** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Share Snapshot** dialog box, select the level-1 organizations to which you want to share the snapshot for the **Organization** parameter.
If you cannot obtain the organization list due to lack of permissions, you can enter the UID of a level-1 organization.
6. Click **OK**.

**View snapshot sharing information**

1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Click the **Share Snapshot** tab to view snapshot sharing information.
**Shared by Me**: View the information about the snapshots that are shared by the current level -1 organization to other level -1 organizations. You
can view the snapshot ID, snapshot name, status, added tags, snapshot source, disk capacity, disk ID, disk name, disk attributes, progress, organization, and resource set of a shared snapshot.
**Shared by Others**: View the information about the snapshots that are shared by other level-1 organizations to the current level-1 organization.
You can view the snapshot ID, snapshot name, status of the instant access feature, disk ID, disk name, disk capacity, encryption status, snapshot source, progress, description, update time, and creation time of a shared snapshot.
5. In the upper-left corner of the snapshot list, enter a keyword in the search box, such as the snapshot name, snapshot ID, disk ID, creation time, or tag
to search for snapshots that meet the filter condition.

**Unshare a snapshot**

You can unshare a snapshot that you no longer need to share with other level -1 organizations.

**Important**

After a snapshot is unshared, an organization that accepted the shared snapshot cannot re-initialize a data disk created from the snapshot.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. On the **Disk Snapshots** tab, find the shared snapshot that you want to manage and click **Share Snapshot** in the **Actions** column.
You can also find the shared snapshot in the **Shared by Me** list on the **Share Snapshot** tab and click **Share Snapshot** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Shared Information** section, find the organization from which you want to unshare the snapshot and click the
icon in the **Actions** column.
6. Click **OK**.

**RAM role-based authorization for encrypted snapshots**

To share an encrypted snapshot to an organization, you must grant the permissions on the relevant CMK to the organization by using a RAM role.
1. Create a RAM role, configure a RAM policy for granting permissions on a CMK of the current organization, and configure a trust policy for attaching
the RAM role to the organization to which you want to share the snapshot. RAM role: Specify AliyunECSShareEncryptSnapshotDefaultRole. The name of the RAM role must be AliyunECSShareEncryptSnapshotDefaultRole. Otherwise, the encrypted snapshot fails to be shared. Custom policy: `{`

```json
  "Version": "1",
  "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
      "Action": "kms:List*",
      "Resource": "acs:kms:<ID of the region in which the CMK resides>:<ID of the organization to which the CMK belongs>:key",
      "Effect": "Allow"
```

`},` `{`

```json
      "Action": [
        "kms:DescribeKey",
        "kms:TagResource",
        "kms:UntagResource",
        "kms:Encrypt",
        "kms:Decrypt",
        "kms:GenerateDataKey"
```

`],`

```json
      "Resource": "acs:kms:<ID of the region in which the CMK resides>:<ID of the organization to which the CMK belongs>:key/<ID of the CM
K>",
      "Effect": "Allow"
```

`}` `]` `}` Trust policy: `{`

```json
  "Version": "1",
  "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": [
          "<UID of the organization to which to share the snapshot>@ecs.aliyuncs.com"
```

`]` `}` `}` `]` `}`
2. Create a RAM-based authorization for the current organization.
For more information, see the **Create RAM-based authorization** section of the "Create a role" topic in the **Enterprise > Permissions > Role**
**Permissions** section of **Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User Guide** .
If you want to customize a snapshot based on your business requirements, you can edit the name and description of the snapshot.

**Prerequisites**

A snapshot is created for a disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot.

After you create snapshots that have the instant access feature enabled for premium performance disks, you can immediately use the snapshots to create or roll back disks. If you no longer need to use the instant access feature for a snapshot, you can manually disable the feature.

The instant access feature is enabled when you create a snapshot for a premium performance disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The instant access feature can be enabled only for snapshots that are created for premium performance disks. The instant access feature cannot be enabled again after it is disabled. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**3.5.1.6. View the snapshot size of a disk based on the snapshot chain of the disk**

A snapshot chain is a chain of all snapshots created for a disk. A disk corresponds to a snapshot chain. You can view the size of all snapshots of a disk based on the snapshot chain of the disk.

**Background information**

The total size of snapshots of a disk is calculated based on the snapshot chain of the disk. A snapshot chain is a chain of all snapshots created for a disk. The total size represents the amount of storage space occupied by the data blocks in all snapshots of the disk. The following section describes snapshot size-related concepts: Full snapshot size: the amount of storage space occupied by all data blocks in a single snapshot. Incremental snapshot size: the amount of storage space occupied by the data blocks that represent the difference between the current snapshot and the previous snapshot in the same snapshot chain. Total snapshot size: the sum of the size of the initial full snapshot and the sizes of all subsequent incremental snapshots.

**Prerequisites**

At least one snapshot is created for a disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The calculation of the snapshot chain size takes several minutes, and the size is only for reference.
1. Log on to the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Click the **Snapshot Chain** tab, select a field from the drop-down list, and enter a keyword in the search box. Then, click the
icon. The snapshot chains that meet the filter condition are displayed in the list. You can search for snapshot chains by using the **Automatic Identification**, **Snapshot Chain ID**, **Source Disk ID**, **Instance ID**, or **Filter**
**by Tag** filter option.
Fuzzy search is supported for the **Snapshot Chain ID**, **Source Disk ID**, and **Instance ID** filter options. You can specify multiple filter conditions to narrow down search results.
5. In the **Snapshot Chain Size** column of the snapshot chain, view the size of all snapshots of the disk.

**Related operations**

After you find the snapshot chain of the disk, you can perform the following operations as required.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| View the details of the snapshot chain | Click the ID of the snapshot chain or clickV iew Details in the Actions column. You can view the information about the snapshots of the disk and perform operations on a snapshot such as editing the snapshot, rolling back the disk by using the snapshot, creating a custom image from the snapshot, and deleting the snapshot. |
| View the information about the instance to which the corresponding disk of the snapshot chain belongs | Click the instance ID in the Instance ID/Name column of the snapshot chain to view the information about the instance to which the corresponding disk of the snapshot chain belongs. |
| View the information about the disk to which the snapshot chain corresponds | Click the disk ID in the Source Disk ID/Name column of the snapshot chain to view the information about the disk to which the snapshot chain corresponds. |

If you have created a snapshot for a disk, you can use the rollback feature to restore the data of the disk to a specific point in time. The disk rollback operation is irreversible. After the disk is rolled back, the data stored on the disk before the operation is performed cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**Prerequisites**

A snapshot of the disk to be rolled back is created, and no other snapshot is being created for the disk. For more information, see Create a snapshot. The disk is not released. The instance to which the disk belongs is in the **Stopped** state.
1. Log in to the ECS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
3. In the top navigation bar, select an organization, a resource set, and a region.
4. Find the snapshot that you want to use to roll back the specified disk and click **Roll Back Disk** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **Roll Back Disk**.

**What to do next**

After a disk is rolled back, the host configuration file and the configurations, such as the hostname, SSH key pair, password, network, system source, and clock source, are initialized. You must reconfigure the settings. If you resized a disk after you created a snapshot for the disk, the size of the disk is also rolled back after you roll back the disk. To make the disk revert to the size before the rollback, you must log on to the instance to resize the file system. For more information, see Resize a disk. You can create a custom image from a snapshot that contains the operating system and data of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance. Then, you can use the custom image to create multiple identical instances.

**Prerequisites**

A system disk snapshot is created. For more information, see Create a snapshot.

**Background information**

Before you create custom images from snapshots, take note of the following items: Notes on snapshots used to create custom images: A custom image can be created from a system disk snapshot or from a system disk snapshot and one or more data disk snapshots. Data disk snapshots alone cannot be used to create custom images. Both encrypted and unencrypted snapshots can be used to create custom images. Notes on custom images: Custom images cannot be used across regions.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.

4. Find a system disk snapshot. If **System Disk** is displayed in the **Disk Type** column corresponding to a snapshot, the snapshot is a system disk
snapshot. In the **Actions** column, click **Create Custom Image**.
5. In the **Create Custom Image** dialog box, configure the parameters as required. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Sharing Scope | Select the scope in which to share the custom image. Valid values: Current Organization and Subordinate Organizations Current Resource Set Current Organization |
| Image Name | Enter a name for the custom image. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, periods (.), underscores (), _ hyphens (-), and colons (:). It must start with a letter. |
| Image Description | Enter a description for the custom image. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https://. |

6. Click **OK**.
In the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) console, you can delete a snapshot that is no longer needed. Deleted snapshots cannot be restored. Proceed with caution. If a system disk snapshot has been used to create a custom image, the snapshot cannot be deleted. Snapshots that have been used to create disks cannot be deleted.
1. Log on to the ECS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Computing > Elastic Compute Service**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Storage & Snapshots > Snapshots**.
